blocks.text: Interview with Jasper Fortuin – Managing Director WorldEmp India: Successfully collaborating with remote teams

In a world where technology is rapidly evolving, working with remote teams is increasingly becoming the norm. Companies are discovering the benefits of remote recruitment, particularly hiring permanent colleagues remotely.
blocks.html: In a world where technology is rapidly evolving, working with remote teams is increasingly becoming the norm. Companies are discovering the benefits of remote recruitment, particularly hiring permanent colleagues remotely.

blocks.text: But what makes these collaborations successful? And why do Dutch companies often choose remote recruitment in countries like India?
blocks.html: But what makes these collaborations successful? And why do Dutch companies often choose remote recruitment in countries like India?

blocks.text: Background and experience of Jasper Fortuin

Jasper Fortuin, Managing Director at WorldEmp India, has extensive experience with remote recruitment and collaboration between Dutch and Indian colleagues. "From 2016 to 2021, I worked for KPN in India and witnessed hundreds of teams collaborating between the Netherlands and India. Since I joined WorldEmp in February 2023, I have met many colleagues and have been impressed by their technical and personal qualities. At WorldEmp, both large and small companies work with Indian colleagues in technical roles, and that collaboration is particularly successful."

At WorldEmp, both large and small companies work with Indian colleagues in technical roles, and that collaboration is particularly successful."

blocks.text: "Understanding and acceptance of cultural differences are crucial. Indian colleagues must truly be part of the team."
The keys to success with remote teams: culture, engagement, and shared successes

What are the keys to success in working with remote teams? "Understanding and acceptance of cultural differences are essential," emphasizes Fortuin. "It’s important to build personal relationships, even virtually, and to truly make Indian colleagues part of the team. It doesn’t work if they are only given less popular tasks; at WorldEmp, we ensure challenging and interesting projects for everyone."

"It’s important to build personal relationships, even virtually, and to truly make Indian colleagues part of the team. blocks.text: Fortuin shares an example of how joint celebrations strengthen a sense of teamwork. "We celebrate successes both in the Netherlands and in India. This can include shared breakfast sessions or distributing gifts in both countries. This way, Indian and Dutch colleagues feel equal, which is essential for effective collaboration."

This can include shared breakfast sessions or distributing gifts in both countries. This way, Indian and Dutch colleagues feel equal, which is essential for effective collaboration."

blocks.text: Language and culture as challenges in Dutch-Indian collaborations

Why does collaboration between Dutch and Indian teams sometimes falter? According to Fortuin, this often stems from misunderstandings related to language and culture. "Many companies still communicate in Dutch, which can be challenging for Indian colleagues. Cultural differences also play a role. In India, for instance, there is a strong sense of hierarchy, making open feedback not always a given. At WorldEmp, we therefore screen candidates not only for technical skills but also for their ability to communicate proactively and clearly in a Dutch work environment."

blocks.text: Background and vision on WorldEmp

Peter van Londen has a background in engineering and management, gained in both the Netherlands and Switzerland, and is a co-founder of WorldEmp. "Efficiency has always been central to my work," says Van Londen.
blocks.html: Peter van Londen has a background in engineering and management, gained in both the Netherlands and Switzerland, and is a co-founder of WorldEmp. "Efficiency has always been central to my work," says Van Londen.

blocks.text: His experience with cultural differences and restructuring international supply chains, particularly during his time in Switzerland, has prepared him well for his current role. "At WorldEmp, we help companies unlock their full potential by providing access to global talent. Our focus is not only on technical skills but also on the cultural fit and social skills of our employees," he explains.

blocks.text: Benefits and Challenges of Remote Teams

Remote employees via WorldEmp offer several advantages, according to Peter, such as cost savings, flexibility, and a larger talent pool with specific technical skills. "One of our clients in the tech sector was able to accelerate their development process by 30% and win projects that would have otherwise been impossible," he explains.

blocks.text: Despite these benefits, working with remote teams also requires a thoughtful approach, especially in terms of communication and cultural sensitivity. "Once cultural differences are under control, the benefits of diversity in teams remain," he concludes.

blocks.text: “Our employees typically work directly on the client’s server, so we do not store customer data ourselves.” WorldEmp implements measures such as regular audits, cybersecurity training, and secure communication channels to ensure safety. “Every decision regarding IT and software is made with data protection in mind.”

blocks.text: The future of remote working

Van Londen views remote working as a lasting trend, especially in the tech sector. “Remote working will become the norm,” he predicts. “Companies will increasingly realize the benefits of global talent, leading to more diversity and innovation.”

blocks.text: In the Netherlands, an increasing number of companies are experiencing the negative effects of labor market shortages. blocks.text: What is a knowledge migrant?

A knowledge migrant is a highly educated foreign employee who comes to the Netherlands to work in a sector with a shortage of highly skilled personnel. These employees possess specific knowledge and skills that are difficult to find in the Netherlands. The Dutch government introduced the knowledge migrant policy to help companies address this shortage. Businesses can relatively easily hire knowledge migrants, provided they meet certain criteria, such as a minimum salary threshold.

blocks.text: Labor market shortages and the role of knowledge migrants

Labor market shortages in the Netherlands are particularly noticeable in technical and IT sectors, but finding qualified personnel is becoming increasingly challenging across other fields as well. Knowledge migrants can play a crucial role in addressing this issue. By recruiting globally, companies gain access to talent that would otherwise remain out of reach. This enables organizations to bring in the right knowledge and expertise, which is essential to remain competitive in a rapidly changing market.

blocks.text: Tips for successful remote cooperation
To overcome these challenges and be successful with a remote team, there are several best practices you can follow.
blocks.html: To overcome these challenges and be successful with a remote team, there are several best practices you can follow.

items: First, it is important to establish clear communication channels. This includes not only choosing the right tools, such as video meetings and chat apps, but also establishing communication guidelines. For example, who should be kept informed of what information, and in what way?

It is also essential to hold regular check-ins and team meetings. This not only helps keep everyone up to date on progress and any problems, but again strengthens team cohesion. Setting clear goals and expectations is also very important. When everyone knows exactly what is expected of them and the deadlines, this can help increase productivity and reduce misunderstandings.

Flexibility and trust are also important. Trust your team members to deliver their work on time and with the right quality, and be flexible with working hours. This can help foster a positive work culture and increase motivation.

blocks.text: Wat is een kennismigrant?

Een kennismigrant is een hoogopgeleide buitenlandse werknemer die naar Nederland komt om te werken in een sector waar een tekort aan hooggekwalificeerd personeel bestaat. Deze werknemers beschikken over specifieke kennis en vaardigheden die in Nederland moeilijk te vinden zijn. De Nederlandse overheid heeft het kennismigrantenbeleid in het leven geroepen om bedrijven te helpen dit tekort aan te vullen. Bedrijven kunnen kennismigranten relatief eenvoudig aannemen, mits zij voldoen aan bepaalde criteria zoals een minimumsalarisgrens.

blocks.text: De krapte op de arbeidsmarkt en de rol van kennismigranten

De krapte op de arbeidsmarkt in Nederland is vooral merkbaar in technische en IT-sectoren, maar ook in andere vakgebieden wordt het vinden van gekwalificeerd personeel steeds lastiger. Kennismigranten kunnen een cruciale rol spelen bij het oplossen van dit probleem. Doordat bedrijven wereldwijd kunnen werven, krijgen zij toegang tot talenten die anders buiten bereik zouden blijven. Dit geeft organisaties de kans om de juiste kennis en expertise in huis te halen, wat essentieel is om concurrerend te blijven in een snel veranderende markt.

blocks.text: Tips voor succesvolle integratie van kennismigranten

Het is belangrijk dat zij weten waar ze terecht kunnen met vragen of problemen en dat er regelmatig feedback wordt gegeven over hun werkprestaties.

Duidelijke informatie over bedrijfswaarden en werkcultuur: het is voor kennismigranten vaak moeilijk om meteen de bedrijfswaarden en werkcultuur te doorgronden. en.title: India Changed Me: A Different Perspective on Talent
en.description: Discover how nearly a year of living and working in India changed Jasper’s perspective on talent, India and international collaboration.

blocks.text: It might change the way you look at talent, too.
Writen by Jasper Fortuin, Managing Director India
blocks.html: Writen by Jasper Fortuin, Managing Director India

blocks.text: If you had told me ten years ago that I would spend almost a decade of my professional life in India, I probably would have smiled politely and changed the subject. Yet here I am. And India has become my second home.
blocks.html: If you had told me ten years ago that I would spend almost a decade of my professional life in India, I probably would have smiled politely and changed the subject. Yet here I am. And India has become my second home.

blocks.text: I started my professional journey in India in November 2016 when I was working for Royal Dutch KPN. What initially felt like an international assignment slowly became something much bigger. After spending five years in India, I returned to the Netherlands in 2021. But India never really left me.
blocks.html: I started my professional journey in India in November 2016 when I was working for Royal Dutch KPN. What initially felt like an international assignment slowly became something much bigger. After spending five years in India, I returned to the Netherlands in 2021. But India never really left me.

blocks.text: Shortly after my return, I started talking with the founders and shareholders of WorldEmp, who I met during my time in India. We shared the same belief: businesses in Europe were overlooking one of the largest pools of highly skilled professionals in the world. At the beginning of 2023, I moved back to Pune, India, where I now lead the Indian operations of WorldEmp. And every day, I become a little more convinced that many Western companies still underestimate what India has become.

We shared the same belief: businesses in Europe were overlooking one of the largest pools of highly skilled professionals in the world. At the beginning of 2023, I moved back to Pune, India, where I now lead the Indian operations of WorldEmp. And every day, I become a little more convinced that many Western companies still underestimate what India has become.

blocks.alt: offshore oil, gas, wind, jack-up, energy transition

blocks.text: The India Most People Don't See

Whenever I visit the Netherlands, conversations about India tend to be remarkably similar. People talk about the horrible traffic, the bureaucracy and the immense inequality. And while none of those topics are entirely inaccurate, they only tell a very small part of the story.
blocks.html: Whenever I visit the Netherlands, conversations about India tend to be remarkably similar. People talk about the horrible traffic, the bureaucracy and the immense inequality. And while none of those topics are entirely inaccurate, they only tell a very small part of the story.

blocks.text: Throughout my years here, I've made it somewhat of a personal mission to challenge the narrative. Not because India is perfect—it certainly isn't—but because the picture many people in Europe have in their minds is hopelessly outdated.
blocks.html: Throughout my years here, I've made it somewhat of a personal mission to challenge the narrative. Not because India is perfect—it certainly isn't—but because the picture many people in Europe have in their minds is hopelessly outdated.

blocks.text: I've travelled extensively across this immense country. I've visited Kerala multiple times, explored Tamil Nadu, spent time in Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi, and even travelled to the Himalayas. Every region feels like a different country; the food changes. They speak a different language. And traditions change.
blocks.html: I've travelled extensively across this immense country. I've visited Kerala multiple times, explored Tamil Nadu, spent time in Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi, and even travelled to the Himalayas. Every region feels like a different country; the food changes. They speak a different language. And traditions change.

blocks.text: The scale of India is difficult to comprehend until you've experienced it yourself. What continuously surprises me is the speed at which things evolve. Entire neighbourhoods transform within a few years. New metro systems emerge. Airports rival those in Europe or the Middle East. Digital payment platforms are used by everyone—from corporate executives to small street vendors.
blocks.html: The scale of India is difficult to comprehend until you've experienced it yourself. What continuously surprises me is the speed at which things evolve. Entire neighbourhoods transform within a few years. New metro systems emerge. Airports rival those in Europe or the Middle East. Digital payment platforms are used by everyone—from corporate executives to small street vendors.

blocks.text: India changes at a very rapid pace.
blocks.html: India changes at a very rapid pace.

blocks.text: However, drive about 100 kilometers into the countryside from any tier-1 city and you’ll see the traditional India; this the India people probably know from the history books; dusty towns with farmers, who struggle to make ends meet.
blocks.html: However, drive about 100 kilometers into the countryside from any tier-1 city and you’ll see the traditional India; this the India people probably know from the history books; dusty towns with farmers, who struggle to make ends meet.

blocks.text: Two Countries Living Side by Side

One of the lessons India taught me is that multiple realities can coexist. On one side, there is the poverty. Even after almost ten years, seeing children living on the streets still affects me. At the same time, there is another India. A growing middle class that is expanding at an astonishing pace. Families buying their first homes. Young professionals travelling abroad. Entrepreneurs building global businesses. Engineers working on products used by millions of people worldwide.

Families buying their first homes. Young professionals travelling abroad. Entrepreneurs building global businesses. Engineers working on products used by millions of people worldwide.

blocks.text: When I walk through one of Pune's modern shopping centres, I sometimes need to remind myself that many Europeans still view India through a lens that belongs to the 1990s. The India I experience every day is young, ambitious, increasingly affluent and exceptionally well educated. And that matters for businesses.

The India I experience every day is young, ambitious, increasingly affluent and exceptionally well educated. And that matters for businesses.

blocks.text: Life Here Is Different. Very Different.

Compared to the Netherlands, almost everything works differently. Some differences make me smile. Others occasionally drive me mad. Take paperwork. Every year, I need to notarise my rental agreement. There are stamps, signatures and procedures that sometimes feel as if they've travelled through time from another century.

Every year, I need to notarise my rental agreement. There are stamps, signatures and procedures that sometimes feel as if they've travelled through time from another century.

blocks.text: Another thing which is different, especially compared with The Netherlands, is authority. Hierarchy plays a huge role here in India. Business owners are glorified; more than often, I’ve seen a statue of the late-founder, in front of the headquarters.

blocks.text: Luckily, there are also areas where India genuinely surprised me in a positive way. Healthcare is one of them. I've been admitted to hospital twice during the last three years. While nobody enjoys being a patient, both experiences left me impressed. The care was excellent. The doctors were highly knowledgeable and the entire approach was remarkably patient-centric.

While nobody enjoys being a patient, both experiences left me impressed. The care was excellent. The doctors were highly knowledgeable and the entire approach was remarkably patient-centric.

blocks.text: Healthcare in India; tiered, but very good

Yes, India has a tiered healthcare system, and access varies greatly depending on financial circumstances. But if you compare the speed, availability and personal attention with some healthcare systems in Europe, there are certainly lessons that can be learned.

blocks.text: And there is a reason why Indian doctors are respected globally. Many people are surprised when I tell them that approximately one in five doctors practising in the United States was born in India.

blocks.text: Endless number of professionals.
Not only doctors. A growing number engineers, architects, project managers. finance professionals.

blocks.text: The Weather Helps Too

There is another reason I enjoy living here; the weather. As a Dutchman, spending most of the year without worrying about freezing temperatures still feels like a luxury. Let's be honest: waking up in January without scraping ice from your car has its advantages. The only exception is the monsoon.
blocks.html: There is another reason I enjoy living here; the weather. As a Dutchman, spending most of the year without worrying about freezing temperatures still feels like a luxury. Let's be honest: waking up in January without scraping ice from your car has its advantages. The only exception is the monsoon.

blocks.text: While many people love it, I remain unconvinced. The endless rain, flooded streets and permanently damp shoes are not among my favourite Indian experiences. But every country has its imperfections.

blocks.text: The India That Keeps Me Here

Over the years, India has given me more than professional opportunities. It has given me friendships. Some of my closest friends here are Indian. Others are expats who decided, just like me, that India deserved more than a temporary visit.
blocks.html: Over the years, India has given me more than professional opportunities. It has given me friendships. Some of my closest friends here are Indian. Others are expats who decided, just like me, that India deserved more than a temporary visit.

blocks.text: These relationships allowed me to see the country beyond business meetings, airports and office buildings. I've attended weddings, celebrated festivals, travelled across states and shared countless dinners discussing everything from cricket to politics. Those experiences changed my perspective. The longer I stay here, the harder it becomes to simplify India into stereotypes.

blocks.text: What This Means for Dutch Businesses

This brings me to a question I often receive from business leaders in the Netherlands: "Why should we consider building a team in India?”. My answer is straightforward: not because labour is cheaper. While cost-efficiency could be there, that argument belongs to the past. The real opportunity is access to talent.

blocks.text: My Conclusion After Nearly Ten Years
When I arrived in India in 2016, I promised myself something simple: Observe first. Judge later.

nl.description: Ontdek hoe bijna tien jaar wonen en werken in India Jasper’s kijk op talent, India en internationale samenwerking heeft veranderd.

blocks.text: Als je me tien jaar geleden had verteld dat ik bijna een decennium van mijn professionele leven in India zou doorbrengen, had ik waarschijnlijk beleefd geglimlacht en het onderwerp veranderd. En toch ben ik hier. India is inmiddels mijn tweede thuis geworden.

blocks.text: Mijn professionele reis in India begon in november 2016, toen ik voor KPN werkte. Wat aanvankelijk voelde als een internationale opdracht, groeide langzaam uit tot iets veel groters. Na vijf jaar in India keerde ik in 2021 terug naar Nederland. Maar India liet me nooit echt los.

blocks.text: Kort na mijn terugkeer raakte ik opnieuw in gesprek met de oprichters en aandeelhouders van WorldEmp, die ik tijdens mijn tijd in India had leren kennen. We deelden dezelfde overtuiging: Europese bedrijven lieten een van de grootste groepen hoogopgeleide professionals ter wereld nog te vaak links liggen. Begin 2023 verhuisde ik terug naar Pune, India, waar ik nu leiding geef aan de Indiase activiteiten van WorldEmp. blocks.text: Het India dat de meeste mensen niet zien

Wanneer ik Nederland bezoek, zijn gesprekken over India opvallend vaak hetzelfde. Mensen hebben het over het verschrikkelijke verkeer, de bureaucratie en de enorme ongelijkheid. En hoewel geen van die onderwerpen volledig onjuist is, vertellen ze slechts een heel klein deel van het verhaal.
blocks.html: Wanneer ik Nederland bezoek, zijn gesprekken over India opvallend vaak hetzelfde. Mensen hebben het over het verschrikkelijke verkeer, de bureaucratie en de enorme ongelijkheid. En hoewel geen van die onderwerpen volledig onjuist is, vertellen ze slechts een heel klein deel van het verhaal.

blocks.text: Door de jaren heen is het voor mij bijna een persoonlijke missie geworden om dat beeld ter discussie te stellen. Niet omdat India perfect is — dat is het zeker niet — maar omdat het beeld dat veel Europeanen van India hebben hopeloos verouderd is.

blocks.text: Ik heb uitgebreid door dit enorme land gereisd. Ik ben meerdere keren in Kerala geweest, heb Tamil Nadu verkend, tijd doorgebracht in Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Mumbai en Delhi en ben zelfs naar de Himalaya gereisd. Elke regio voelt als een ander land. Het eten verandert. Er wordt een andere taal gesproken. En ook tradities verschillen.

Het eten verandert. Er wordt een andere taal gesproken. En ook tradities verschillen.

blocks.text: De omvang van India is moeilijk te bevatten totdat je het zelf hebt ervaren. Wat me steeds weer verbaast, is de snelheid waarmee het land verandert. Hele wijken veranderen binnen een paar jaar. Nieuwe metrolijnen verschijnen. Luchthavens kunnen zich meten met die in Europa of het Midden-Oosten. Digitale betaalplatforms worden door iedereen gebruikt — van bestuurders van grote bedrijven tot kleine straatverkopers.

blocks.text: Twee landen naast elkaar

Een van de belangrijkste lessen die India mij heeft geleerd, is dat meerdere werkelijkheden naast elkaar kunnen bestaan. Aan de ene kant is er armoede. Zelfs na bijna tien jaar raakt het me nog steeds wanneer ik kinderen op straat zie leven.

en.title: Professor Maarten Steinbuch joins WorldEmp's Advisory Board
en.description: Miscommunication, knowledge that never accumulates and too little focus on customer value are the biggest problems companies run into when outsourcing.

blocks.text: Professor Maarten Steinbuch joins WorldEmp's Advisory Board

Maarten Steinbuch, professor in high-tech systems and an entrepreneur, has joined WorldEmp. Steinbuch is taking a seat on the commercial Advisory Board. WorldEmp is honoured that an absolute authority such as Steinbuch is making his knowledge and network available to the company. Director Frank Korf: “That a figurehead like Maarten has so much confidence in our concept of connecting remote talent to Dutch companies makes us tremendously proud.”

Maarten Steinbuch (61) has, as he puts it himself, a fascination with everything that moves. Self-driving cars, scanners, precision medical robots, machines for the chip industry - with his team at TU/e in Eindhoven, Steinbuch has worked on all kinds of groundbreaking innovations. He is, accordingly, a respected spider in the web of Brainport Eindhoven, the alliance of technological and innovative companies in the Eindhoven region.

Now he is joining the commercial Advisory Board of WorldEmp, a company that focuses not on robots and machines but on people. That is no contradiction, according to Steinbuch. On the contrary. “Human capital is incredibly important in the manufacturing industry around Eindhoven. That has always interested me too. I have also always worked to get more people interested in engineering, for instance through the Techniekpromotie foundation, where we challenge young children with the First Lego League, and now through the capstone of my career, Eindhoven Engine, where we bring people together to stimulate innovation. But a great deal is also invested in training people at TU/e and at the companies themselves. A great many are needed. A company like ASML alone has six thousand vacancies. That is five hundred a month. That cannot be done from your own intake. A company like WorldEmp can play a part in filling those vacancies. And I want to make my contribution to that.”

Steinbuch came into contact with WorldEmp on a trade mission to India with the Royal Family, and was impressed by WorldEmp's concept of remote working, in which staff in India are connected to Dutch companies through a digital platform. “The idea that you put the potential in other countries to work for the Dutch economy, in a smart way with remote working, appeals to me a great deal. WorldEmp's way of recruiting safeguards the quality. There is a lot of attention for soft skills too.
“The way WorldEmp is set up, it is as though the employee is sitting in your office.”

“Because of the covid pandemic there is a much greater awareness at companies that working remotely is interesting too,” Steinbuch observes. “The way WorldEmp is set up, it is as though the employee is sitting in your office. You really do create a digital knowledge migrant. Companies have seen by now that efficiency has not dropped through working remotely. And by bringing these highly educated people together digitally from around the world, problem-solving capacity rises in leaps.” Taking a seat on WorldEmp's commercial Advisory Board naturally also means Steinbuch will give advice, asked for and unasked. He has already given one apparently simple piece: “I saw that mechatronics was nowhere on the website as a discipline, something that is very important in the Eindhoven area. We are going to add that, and I am glad to help with the exact wording.” But Steinbuch wants to do much more. “Every year dozens of Indian students come to Eindhoven to be trained. But at a certain point they want to go back to India after all. Understandable, but a waste for our region. I want to see whether we can keep them for Dutch companies through WorldEmp's concept.”

Because that is how Steinbuch sees his connection with WorldEmp: it has to cut both ways. Companies in the technology sector should benefit from the collaboration too. “WorldEmp is not going to solve all the sector's problems either. Everyone understands that. I worry about vocationally trained staff, for example. But WorldEmp can contribute to solutions at bachelor's and master's level. And even if that is only a little, it has an enormous positive effect on the earning power of the manufacturing industry. That really does have an impact on society.”

blocks.text: What is Offshoring?

Offshoring is the process by which companies move their operations or services to another country, often to save costs or gain access to a specialized labor market. In the IT sector, offshoring typically involves outsourcing IT services, such as software development or technical support, to countries where labor costs are lower, such as India, the Philippines, or Eastern Europe.

In the IT sector, offshoring typically involves outsourcing IT services, such as software development or technical support, to countries where labor costs are lower, such as India, the Philippines, or Eastern Europe.

blocks.text: Advantages and Disadvantages of Offshore IT Outsourcing

blocks.text: Advantages:
blocks.html: Advantages:

items: Cost savings: One of the biggest benefits of offshore IT outsourcing is the significant savings on labor costs. IT specialists in countries like India typically earn less than their counterparts in Western countries, without compromising on quality.
Access to specialized talent: Offshore outsourcing gives companies access to a broader pool of highly skilled IT professionals, often with expertise in the latest technologies.
24/7 productivity: By deploying offshore teams in different time zones, companies can benefit from continuous production and faster project completion.

blocks.text: Disadvantages:
blocks.html: Disadvantages:

items: Communication challenges: Working with teams in other countries can lead to language and cultural barriers, which can complicate communication.
Quality control: Ensuring quality can be challenging when teams are geographically dispersed. Companies must establish clear processes for quality assurance.

blocks.text: Tips for successful remote cooperation
To overcome these challenges and be successful with a remote team, there are several best practices you can follow.
blocks.html: To overcome these challenges and be successful with a remote team, there are several best practices you can follow.

items: First, it is important to establish clear communication channels. This includes not only choosing the right tools, such as video meetings and chat apps, but also establishing communication guidelines. For example, who should be kept informed of what information, and in what way?

It is also essential to hold regular check-ins and team meetings. This not only helps keep everyone up to date on progress and any problems, but again strengthens team cohesion. Setting clear goals and expectations is also very important. When everyone knows exactly what is expected of them and the deadlines, this can help increase productivity and reduce misunderstandings.

Flexibility and trust are also important. Trust your team members to deliver their work on time and with the right quality, and be flexible with working hours. This can help foster a positive work culture and increase motivation.

blocks.text: Wat is offshoring?

Offshoring is het proces waarbij bedrijven hun activiteiten of diensten naar een ander land verplaatsen, vaak om kosten te besparen of toegang te krijgen tot een gespecialiseerde arbeidsmarkt. In de IT-sector betekent offshoring vaak het uitbesteden van IT-diensten, zoals softwareontwikkeling of technische ondersteuning, aan landen waar de arbeidskosten lager zijn, zoals India, de Filipijnen of Oost-Europa.

blocks.text: By: Peter van Londen, COO WorldEmp

blocks.text: ISO 42001 in practice: from engineering to data governance
A Sustainable Alternative: Digital Knowledge Migrants
Governance and architecture
In the area of governance and architecture, we have achieved the following results:
blocks.html: In the area of governance and architecture, we have achieved the following results:

items: We have developed a comprehensive AI Implementation High-Level Architecture & Design Playbook. This links ISO 42001 requirements to practical controls, a cloud-native architecture based on technologies such as Azure, AKS, Next.js and FastAPI, and a gated AI lifecycle delivery model.
We have set up clear governance structures, including RACI matrices and reference architectures for scalable, secure and ethical AI SaaS delivery.

blocks.text: Responsible AI Impact Assessment

items: For our generative AI SaaS environment, we have carried out a comprehensive Responsible AI Impact Assessment:
This assessment covers, among other things, stakeholder mapping, fairness, privacy, human oversight and risk mitigations.
The approach is fully aligned with the Microsoft Responsible AI Standard and ISO 42001.

blocks.text: Risk and incident management

items: Risk and incidents are structurally embedded in our AIMS:

We have created AI Impact Assessment Registers and Risk Assessment & Treatment Templates to systematically identify, evaluate and mitigate risks. This includes risks related to bias, privacy, security, reliability, operations and regulation.
We have implemented an Information Security Incident & Investigation Framework with AI-specific enhancements, automated reporting and root cause analysis workflows.

blocks.text: Our approach and principles

items: Three principles are central to our approach:
Human-in-the-loop oversight for high-impact decisions.
Continuous monitoring, incident response and improvement cycles.
Transparent stakeholder communication and clear disclosure of AI interactions.

blocks.text: Summary and what comes next
In roughly two weeks, my next blog will explain how we translate this approach into engineering, quality assurance, operational excellence, training, guardrails and data governance.

blocks.text: What is outsource software development?

Outsource software development involves outsourcing software development projects to an external partner. This can involve complete project takeovers or specific parts of a project. Companies often opt for outsourcing when they lack internal resources or want to benefit from specialist knowledge that is not readily available within their organisation. With outsourcing, you can achieve a more flexible, cost-efficient and innovative development process.

blocks.text: Benefits of Outsourcing and Why Outsource Software Development?

blocks.html: Outsourcing offers countless advantages for companies, especially in the competitive technology industry. Here are some of the main reasons why companies choose to outsource software development:

items: Access to Global Expertise: By outsourcing software development, your company gains access to a larger, or even global, talent pool. You can collaborate with experts specializing in the latest technologies and software solutions, leading to more innovative and high-quality products.

Focus on Core Activities: By entrusting software development to an external party, your internal teams can fully focus on their core activities and strategic goals, ensuring that daily operations continue smoothly. This leads to increased efficiency and effectiveness within your organization.

Solving Labor Market Issues: The tight labor market, especially in technical sectors, makes it challenging to find qualified personnel. Outsourcing offers a solution by providing access to a broader talent pool, allowing your company to operate more flexibly and scale effectively while still serving your customers.

Increased Focus on Cybersecurity: With the rise of cyber threats, companies are paying more attention to security-focused software development practices. Choosing an outsourcing partner who specializes in cybersecurity is crucial for protecting your data.

Adoption of Agile and DevOps: Companies are increasingly adopting Agile and DevOps methodologies to enhance efficiency and collaboration in software development. An outsourcing partner who employs these methods can help deliver projects faster and more flexibly.

blocks.text: Peter van Wessel on tank storage: “The fuel of the future is people”

The tank storage sector faces significant challenges. The world is growing more complex, the energy transition demands adaptation, and finding the right people is getting harder. For Peter van Wessel that is not an abstract story. He worked in the port sector for years and is now involved with the Dutch tank storage sector as a business partner and ambassador for WorldEmp.

On the North Sea Canal at Velsen he talks about what appeals to him in this sector, the developments he sees, and why he believes international professionals working remotely can be a practical solution for some companies.
A Sustainable Alternative: Digital Knowledge Migrants
Jasper’s experience
blocks.html: Jasper’s experience

blocks.text: “International professionals from India can significantly accelerate the growth of Dutch and European organisations,” Jasper explains. “At WorldEmp, we very consciously look beyond technical skills alone. Of course, knowledge and experience need to be right, but just as important is the question of how someone fits in with working with the Dutch in practice. That is why we also discussed the well known Dutch directness at the table. In our selection and onboarding processes, we always address cultural differences explicitly. Not because one culture is better than another, but because it helps if colleagues working at a distance understand how we communicate, plan and give feedback. In the end, it is about cultural intelligence: can you move smoothly between different ways of working and still function as one team?”

blocks.text: Trend 1: Digitalization and Automation

blocks.text: AI-send talent acquisition

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the way companies attract and select talent. AI can assist in matching resumes with job openings by using advanced algorithms. This allows recruiters to quickly create a shortlist of the best candidates, saving time and reducing the likelihood of a poor match.

blocks.text: Additionally, companies can build their own database by using AI tools that continuously analyze and store resumes. Digitalisering en automatisering spelen een steeds grotere rol in het recruitmentproces. Bedrijven investeren in technologieën om het wervingsproces efficiënter te maken, waardoor tijd en kosten worden bespaard.
blocks.html: Digitalisering en automatisering spelen een steeds grotere rol in het recruitmentproces. Bedrijven investeren in technologieën om het wervingsproces efficiënter te maken, waardoor tijd en kosten worden bespaard.

blocks.text: AI-gestuurde talent acquisitie

Artificial Intelligence (AI) verandert de manier waarop bedrijven talent aantrekken en selecteren. AI kan helpen bij het matchen van cv’s met vacatures door gebruik te maken van geavanceerde algoritmen. Dit zorgt ervoor dat recruiters snel een shortlist kunnen maken van de beste kandidaten, wat tijd bespaart en de kans op een verkeerde match verkleint.
blocks.html: Artificial Intelligence (AI) verandert de manier waarop bedrijven talent aantrekken en selecteren. AI kan helpen bij het matchen van cv’s met vacatures door gebruik te maken van geavanceerde algoritmen. Dit zorgt ervoor dat recruiters snel een shortlist kunnen maken van de beste kandidaten, wat tijd bespaart en de kans op een verkeerde match verkleint.

blocks.text: Daarnaast kunnen bedrijven hun eigen databank opzetten door gebruik te maken van AI-tools die continu cv’s analyseren en opslaan. Dit biedt toegang tot een constante stroom van potentiële kandidaten, zelfs voordat er een vacature is. Toch is het belangrijk om te onthouden dat, ondanks de voordelen van AI, de menselijke kant van recruitment nooit volledig vervangen kan worden. AI kan helpen bij het sorteren en analyseren van data, maar menselijke recruiters blijven essentieel om de juiste culturele fit en soft skills te beoordelen.

blocks.text: Voordelen voor bedrijven

Bedrijven die digitaliseren en automatiseren in hun recruitmentproces profiteren van diverse voordelen. Ten eerste wordt het wervingsproces efficiënter, omdat repetitieve taken worden geautomatiseerd. Hierdoor kunnen recruiters zich meer richten op strategische taken zoals het voeren van diepgaande interviews en het evalueren van de bedrijfscultuur. Ten tweede leidt automatisering tot een betere kandidatenervaring. Kandidaten ontvangen sneller feedback, wat hun ervaring met het bedrijf verbetert.

De arbeidsmarkt verandert voortdurend, en bedrijven die zich snel kunnen aanpassen hebben een duidelijke voorsprong. Flexibiliteit in het recruitmentproces is essentieel om in te spelen op deze veranderingen.

blocks.text: Trend 3: Diversiteit, gelijkheid en inclusie

Diversiteit, gelijkheid en inclusie (DEI) zijn tegenwoordig een cruciaal onderdeel van een succesvol recruitmentproces. Bedrijven die zich richten op inclusiviteit hebben vaak een diverser en creatiever personeelsbestand. Deze bedrijven zijn beter in staat om problemen vanuit verschillende invalshoeken te benaderen, wat leidt tot betere bedrijfsresultaten.

blocks.text: Trend 4: De opkomst van remote recruitment en werken op afstand

Dit maakt remote recruitment een aantrekkelijke optie voor veel organisaties.

blocks.text: The rise of remote engineers gives companies a good way to work faster, more flexibly and more cost-effectively. Particularly now that demand for good mechanical engineers is rising worldwide, bringing in remote specialists is a smart and durable solution.
In this blog we explain what a remote engineer does, why companies increasingly choose this option, and why WorldEmp is the right partner to start with.
What does a remote engineer do?

A remote engineer works from another location - often internationally - but is fully integrated into the client's team. Thanks to modern communication technology, a remote engineer can collaborate on projects effectively, as though they were in the office.
Tasks and responsibilities of a remote engineer

items: Designing and modelling technical components
Analysing and improving designs and systems
Technical support and project management
Documenting and reporting technical specifications
Working with internal and external stakeholders

blocks.text: Secondment is a way to organise extra capacity, knowledge and continuity without immediately hiring someone directly into permanent employment. A professional works for a client organisation, while the formal employment relationship or contractual arrangement is managed through another party. In the Netherlands, this is often done through a secondment agency, also known as a detacheringsbureau.

blocks.text: What is secondment? What does it mean?

Secondment means that an employee or professional is temporarily or structurally assigned to another department, organisation or client. A seconded employee works in another team or company, while the formal employment or contractual relationship remains with another party.

blocks.text: The secondment meaning is therefore simple: making a professional available to another working environment, with clear agreements about work, responsibility and duration.
blocks.html: The secondment meaning is therefore simple: making a professional available to another working environment, with clear agreements about work, responsibility and duration.

blocks.text: In this context, detached meaning does not mean emotionally distant. It means placed with another organisation, department or client for a defined assignment.

blocks.text: Secondment comes in different forms. Some are temporary and local. Others are international, strategic or fully digital.

blocks.text: Cross departmental secondment

Cross departmental secondment means that an employee temporarily moves to another department within the same company. This can support knowledge sharing, personal development or temporary capacity needs.
blocks.html: Cross departmental secondment means that an employee temporarily moves to another department within the same company. This can support knowledge sharing, personal development or temporary capacity needs.

blocks.text: For example, a data analyst may work with operations for three months to improve reporting. The employer remains the same, but the daily working environment changes for a defined period.

blocks.text: External secondment

External secondment means that an employee works for a different company or host employer for a certain amount of time. This is the classic model of a secondment agency. The client supervises the daily work, while the agency manages selection, guidance and often the formal employment relationship.

blocks.text: International secondment

Client secondment means that a professional works directly within a client organisation for a specified period. This can be useful for the work itself, but also for building the relationship between client and supplier.

blocks.text: What is the law around secondment in the Netherlands?
In the Netherlands, secondment often falls under rules for making workers available to another organisation. The most important law is the Waadi, the Workers Allocation by Intermediaries Act.
blocks.html: In the Netherlands, secondment often falls under rules for making workers available to another organisation. The most important law is the Waadi, the Workers Allocation by Intermediaries Act.

blocks.text: The Waadi covers registration, equal treatment and the non obstruction rule. A party that makes workers available must be correctly registered. Business.gov.nl states that a hirer must check whether the lender is registered in the KVK Business Register and must ensure equal working conditions for hired and salaried employees.
blocks.html: The Waadi covers registration, equal treatment and the non obstruction rule. A party that makes workers available must be correctly registered. Business.gov.nl states that a hirer must check whether the lender is registered in the KVK Business Register and must ensure equal working conditions for hired and salaried employees.

blocks.text: This is often referred to as equal pay and equal working conditions. The principle means that a seconded employee should receive employment conditions that are aligned with comparable employees at the hirer.
blocks.html: This is often referred to as equal pay and equal working conditions. The principle means that a seconded employee should receive employment conditions that are aligned with comparable employees at the hirer.

blocks.text: The KVK registration check, also called the Waadi check, is therefore important. KVK explains that the Waadi aims to protect workers and that organisations can use the Waadi check to see whether a company complies with the registration requirement.

blocks.text: The belemmeringsverbod, or non obstruction rule, is also relevant. In simple terms, the lender may not prevent a seconded employee from entering into direct employment with the hirer after the assignment period, subject to the applicable legal conditions.

nl.title: Detachering uitgelegd: betekenis, vormen, wetgeving en het WorldEmp-model
nl.description: Wat is detachering en hoe werkt het? Lees over de betekenis, de vormen, de voordelen, de Nederlandse wetgeving en hoe WorldEmp digitale detachering organiseert.

blocks.text: Wat is detachering, hoe werkt het en waarom kiezen steeds meer organisaties voor dedicated professionals als structurele uitbreiding van hun team?

Detachering is een manier om extra capaciteit, kennis en continuïteit te organiseren zonder meteen iemand in vaste dienst te nemen. Een professional werkt voor een opdrachtgever, terwijl het formele dienstverband of de contractuele afspraak via een andere partij loopt. In Nederland gebeurt dat vaak via een detacheringsbureau.

Bij WorldEmp geven we detachering een digitale en internationale vorm. Onze professionals werken op afstand, maar zijn dedicated aan het team van de opdrachtgever. De opdrachtgever houdt de regie over het werk, de prioriteiten en de dagelijkse aansturing. Wij verzorgen de selectie, de begeleiding en de continuïteit.

blocks.alt: offshore oil, gas, wind, jack-up, energy transition

blocks.text: Ruim tien jaar geleden zagen we een patroon dat veel organisaties vandaag nog steeds herkennen. Bedrijven willen groeien, projecten versnellen en kwaliteit vasthouden, maar lopen aan tegen een gebrek aan beschikbaar talent. Niet omdat er geen werk is, maar omdat de juiste mensen moeilijk te vinden zijn.

Technisch specialisten, engineers, developers, dataspecialisten, document controllers en projectondersteuners zijn schaars. Lokaal werven duurt vaak te lang. Traditionele outsourcing kan te ver van de dagelijkse praktijk af staan. Een uitzendbureau helpt bij korte pieken, maar biedt niet altijd de continuïteit die structureel werk vraagt.

Daarom zijn we WorldEmp begonnen. Niet als projectleverancier, maar als manier om organisaties structureel te verbinden met dedicated professionals die onderdeel worden van het team. De opdrachtgever houdt de regie over het werk. De professional werkt op afstand, spreekt uitstekend Engels en wordt geselecteerd op expertise, betrouwbaarheid en samenwerking.

Detachering is geen snelle oplossing. Goed georganiseerd is het een praktische manier om capaciteit voor de lange termijn op te bouwen. Dat is vooral relevant voor bedrijven die internationaal werken, meerdere projecten tegelijk draaien of moeite hebben om lokaal voldoende gekwalificeerde mensen te vinden.

In de kern is detachering een driepartijenmodel. Er is de uitlener, meestal het detacheringsbureau. Er is de inlener, de opdrachtgever. En er is de medewerker, de gedetacheerde. De professional werkt in de praktijk voor de opdrachtgever, maar is formeel verbonden aan de uitlener of werkt binnen een afgesproken contractuele structuur.

Dat vraagt om duidelijke afspraken. Denk aan rol, aansturing, arbeidsomstandigheden, veiligheid, geheimhouding, toegang tot data en de duur van de opdracht. Zijn die afspraken helder, dan gaat de samenwerking voelen als een verlengstuk van het interne team.

Bij WorldEmp is dit model digitaal ingericht. De professional reist niet elke dag naar kantoor, maar werkt op afstand als vast onderdeel van jouw team. Dat maakt het model schaalbaar, internationaal en efficiënt. Het past bij organisaties die niet alleen vandaag iemand zoeken, maar capaciteit willen opbouwen voor de jaren daarna.
Wat is detachering? Wat betekent het?

Detachering betekent dat een medewerker of professional tijdelijk of structureel wordt toegewezen aan een andere afdeling, organisatie of opdrachtgever. Een gedetacheerde medewerker werkt in een ander team of bedrijf, terwijl het formele dienstverband of de contractuele relatie bij een andere partij blijft.
De betekenis van detachering is dus eenvoudig: een professional beschikbaar stellen aan een andere werkomgeving, met heldere afspraken over werk, verantwoordelijkheid en duur.
‘Gedetacheerd’ betekent in deze context niet dat iemand op afstand staat. Het betekent dat iemand voor een afgebakende opdracht is geplaatst bij een andere organisatie, afdeling of opdrachtgever.
Detachering kent verschillende vormen. Sommige zijn tijdelijk en lokaal. Andere zijn internationaal, strategisch of volledig digitaal.
Detachering tussen afdelingen

Detachering tussen afdelingen betekent dat een medewerker tijdelijk naar een andere afdeling binnen hetzelfde bedrijf gaat. Dat kan kennisdeling, persoonlijke ontwikkeling of tijdelijke capaciteitsbehoefte ondersteunen.

Een data-analist kan bijvoorbeeld drie maanden bij operations werken om de rapportage te verbeteren. De werkgever blijft dezelfde, maar de dagelijkse werkomgeving verandert voor een afgebakende periode.
Externe detachering

Externe detachering betekent dat een medewerker voor een bepaalde tijd bij een ander bedrijf of een inlenende werkgever werkt. Dit is het klassieke model van het detacheringsbureau. De opdrachtgever stuurt het dagelijkse werk aan, terwijl het bureau de selectie, de begeleiding en vaak het formele werkgeverschap verzorgt.
Dit model wordt vaak gebruikt wanneer een organisatie specialistische kennis nodig heeft, maar iemand niet direct in dienst kan of wil nemen.
Internationale detachering
Internationale detachering betekent dat een professional werkt voor een vestiging, opdrachtgever of partnerorganisatie in het buitenland. Dat kan fysiek ter plaatse, maar ook digitaal.

Het voordeel van internationale detachering is toegang tot internationale kennis en capaciteit. Tegelijk vraagt het om heldere afspraken over toepasselijk recht, belastingen, werktijden, databeveiliging en communicatie.
Detachering bij non-profitorganisaties
Soms worden professionals tijdelijk toegewezen aan goede doelen of non-profitorganisaties. Dat kan waardevol zijn voor kennisoverdracht, leiderschapsontwikkeling en maatschappelijke impact.
Voor medewerkers kan dit een manier zijn om ervaring op te doen in een andere context. Voor organisaties kan het tijdelijk toegang geven tot kennis die intern niet beschikbaar is.
Detachering bij de opdrachtgever

Detachering bij de opdrachtgever betekent dat een professional voor een bepaalde periode rechtstreeks binnen de organisatie van de klant werkt. Dat kan nuttig zijn voor het werk zelf, maar ook voor het opbouwen van de relatie tussen opdrachtgever en leverancier.
De professional leert de processen, systemen en cultuur van de opdrachtgever kennen. Dat zorgt voor sterkere samenwerking en meer wederzijds begrip.

Digitale detachering is de vorm waarin WorldEmp gespecialiseerd is. De professional werkt op afstand, maar is dedicated aan jouw organisatie. Geen losse uitbesteding. Geen anonieme capaciteit. Geen project dat op afstand wordt opgeleverd.
Je krijgt er een collega bij, digitaal. De professional schuift aan bij overleggen, werkt in jouw systemen, volgt jouw prioriteiten en wordt aangestuurd door jouw team.
Daarmee is digitale detachering geschikt voor rollen als:

items: Engineers en ontwerpers
Developers en dataspecialisten
Document controllers
Planners en werkvoorbereiders
Projectondersteuning en technische administratie

blocks.text: Het model werkt vooral goed wanneer organisaties structureel extra capaciteit nodig hebben en niet steeds opnieuw willen beginnen met kortdurende inhuur.
Werken via een detacheringsbureau, hoe is dat?

Werken via een detacheringsbureau betekent dat drie belangen goed met elkaar verbonden moeten worden. De opdrachtgever wil kwaliteit, snelheid en betrouwbaarheid. De professional wil duidelijkheid, ontwikkeling en respect. Het bureau moet ervoor zorgen dat beide kanten goed bij elkaar passen.
Een goed detacheringsbureau doet meer dan cv's doorsturen. Het kijkt naar technische ervaring, communicatie, beschikbaarheid, werkhouding en culturele aansluiting.
Bij WorldEmp is dat opgebouwd rond vijf waarden:

items: Samenwerking met de mens centraal
Professionele betrouwbaarheid
Internationale verbinding
Innovatieve oplossingen
Handelen in plaats van afwachten

blocks.text: Deze waarden doen ertoe in de praktijk. Een professional op afstand moet niet alleen technisch sterk zijn. Hij of zij moet ook helder communiceren, verantwoordelijkheid nemen en passen bij de manier waarop de opdrachtgever werkt.

Daarom investeren we tijd in selectie, onboarding en begeleiding. De samenwerking moet vanaf het begin duidelijk zijn. Wie stuurt het werk aan? Welke systemen worden gebruikt? Hoe vaak is er overleg? Welke resultaten worden verwacht? Hoe wordt de voortgang besproken?
Hoe sterker dat fundament, hoe sneller een professional onderdeel wordt van het team.

Voor een detacheringsbureau betekent het detacheren van personeel verantwoordelijkheid nemen voor de kwaliteit van de match en de afspraken daaromheen. Het bureau moet zorgen voor zorgvuldige selectie, heldere verwachtingen, correcte registratie, transparante afspraken en begeleiding tijdens de samenwerking.
In het driepartijenmodel is het bureau de uitlener. De opdrachtgever is de inlener. De professional is de medewerker of specialist die het werk uitvoert.

In Nederland speelt de Waadi, de Wet allocatie arbeidskrachten door intermediairs, een belangrijke rol. Deze wet geldt voor partijen die arbeidskrachten ter beschikking stellen aan een andere organisatie. Voorlichting van de Rijksoverheid legt uit dat bedrijven die personeel inlenen via detachering te maken hebben met de Waadi-regels voor het in- en uitlenen van personeel.
Een detacheringsbureau moet dus meer zijn dan commercieel effectief. Het moet ook zorgvuldig omgaan met compliance, arbeidsomstandigheden en transparantie.
Wat betekent detachering voor de medewerker?

Voor de medewerker betekent detachering werken in een professionele omgeving, vaak met afwisseling en ontwikkelmogelijkheden. De medewerker doet ervaring op bij een opdrachtgever, leert nieuwe systemen kennen en bouwt expertise op.
Tegelijk vraagt detachering om zelfstandigheid. Zeker bij digitale detachering moet de professional helder communiceren, afspraken nakomen en actief onderdeel worden van het team.

Goede begeleiding is daarom belangrijk. Denk aan loopbaanbegeleiding, persoonlijke ontwikkeling, feedbackmomenten en duidelijke afspraken over werktijden, hybride of remote werken, rapportage en verwachtingen.

Voor veel professionals is digitale detachering aantrekkelijk omdat ze internationaal kunnen werken zonder te verhuizen. Ze krijgen toegang tot professionele opdrachtgevers, uitdagend werk en langdurige samenwerking, terwijl ze in hun eigen omgeving blijven wonen.
Voordelen van detachering voor bedrijven

Het belangrijkste voordeel van detachering voor bedrijven is duidelijk: extra capaciteit zonder een lang lokaal wervingstraject. Dat is waardevol wanneer projecten doorlopen, deadlines naderen en interne teams al onder druk staan.
Detachering helpt bedrijven bij:

items: Sneller opschalen in een krappe arbeidsmarkt
Meer continuïteit dan kortdurende inhuur
Toegang tot specialistische kennis
Minder druk op vaste teams
Betere voorspelbaarheid in planning en capaciteit

blocks.text: Bij WorldEmp gaat detachering niet over het uitbesteden van projecten. De opdrachtgever houdt de regie. De professional werkt onder aansturing van de opdrachtgever.

Dat onderscheid doet ertoe. Veel organisaties willen de regie over hun processen, data of kwaliteit niet kwijtraken. Ze zoeken geen leverancier die het werk overneemt. Ze zoeken mensen die structureel met hen meewerken. Precies daar voegt digitale detachering waarde toe.
Voordelen van detachering voor medewerkers

Voor medewerkers biedt detachering toegang tot nieuwe kennis, internationale opdrachtgevers en professionele ontwikkeling. Ze leren werken in verschillende omgevingen en bouwen ervaring op met uiteenlopende systemen, processen en teams.

Detachering kan ook duidelijkheid geven. Een professional weet voor welke opdrachtgever hij of zij werkt, wat de rol inhoudt en welke afspraken gelden. Zeker bij langere opdrachten is er ruimte om echt onderdeel van het team te worden.

Bij digitale detachering komt daar een voordeel bij. De professional kan internationaal werken zonder fysiek te verhuizen. Dat maakt het model menselijker en duurzamer. Talent krijgt meer kansen. Organisaties krijgen toegang tot een bredere arbeidsmarkt.
Wat zegt de wet over detachering in Nederland?

In Nederland valt detachering vaak onder de regels voor het ter beschikking stellen van arbeidskrachten aan een andere organisatie. De belangrijkste wet is de Waadi, de Wet allocatie arbeidskrachten door intermediairs.

De Waadi gaat over registratie, gelijke behandeling en het belemmeringsverbod. Een partij die arbeidskrachten ter beschikking stelt, moet correct geregistreerd zijn. Business.gov.nl stelt dat een inlener moet controleren of de uitlener is ingeschreven in het KVK Handelsregister en moet zorgen voor gelijke arbeidsvoorwaarden voor ingeleende en eigen medewerkers.

Dit wordt vaak aangeduid als gelijk loon en gelijke arbeidsvoorwaarden. Het principe houdt in dat een gedetacheerde medewerker arbeidsvoorwaarden hoort te krijgen die aansluiten bij vergelijkbare medewerkers bij de inlener.

De controle op KVK-registratie, ook wel de Waadi-check genoemd, is daarom belangrijk. KVK legt uit dat de Waadi bedoeld is om werknemers te beschermen en dat organisaties met de Waadi-check kunnen zien of een bedrijf aan de registratieplicht voldoet.

Ook het belemmeringsverbod is relevant. Eenvoudig gezegd mag de uitlener een gedetacheerde medewerker niet beletten om na de opdracht rechtstreeks in dienst te treden bij de inlener, binnen de geldende wettelijke voorwaarden.

Er kunnen ook andere onderwerpen spelen, zoals inlenersaansprakelijkheid voor loonheffingen, cao-bepalingen, de Arbeidstijdenwet, reiskostenvergoeding, thuiswerken of hybride werken en secundaire voorwaarden zoals een leaseauto bij lokale bureaumodellen. De precieze toepassing hangt af van de structuur, het land, de rol en de afspraken tussen partijen.

Ook het juridische landschap verandert. De Rijksoverheid meldt dat de Wtta, de Wet toelating terbeschikkingstelling van arbeidskrachten, op 1 januari 2027 in werking treedt en strengere regels introduceert voor uitleners van personeel.
Dat maakt een zorgvuldige inrichting belangrijk. Niet alleen voor het detacheringsbureau, maar ook voor de opdrachtgever die met dat bureau werkt.
Kosten van detachering

De kosten van detachering hangen af van de rol, het ervaringsniveau, de beschikbaarheid, de looptijd, de locatie en de begeleiding. Bij lokale detacheringsmodellen kan het tarief marge, werkgeverslasten, reiskostenvergoeding, een leaseauto, inlenersaansprakelijkheid en cao-verplichtingen omvatten.

Bij digitale detachering kun je beter verder kijken dan het uurtarief. De echte vraag is wat structurele capaciteit in totaal oplevert. Denk aan minder vertraging, minder druk op senior medewerkers, betere continuïteit en minder tijdverlies door steeds opnieuw kortdurende krachten in te werken.
Dit onderwerp verdient een apart artikel over contract en geld. Voor deze pagina is de kernvraag eenvoudig: wat kost de professional, en wat kost het als het werk niet gedaan wordt?
Detacheringscontract en detacheringsovereenkomst
Een goed detacheringscontract of een goede detacheringsovereenkomst maakt verwachtingen concreet. Het voorkomt misverstanden en beschermt alle partijen.
Belangrijke onderdelen zijn onder meer:

items: Rol, taken en verantwoordelijkheden
Looptijd van de opdracht en opzegtermijn
Tarief, facturatie en kosten
Geheimhouding, data en beveiliging
Aansturing, werktijden en rapportage

blocks.text: Vaak is er ook een opdrachtbevestiging of plaatsingsovereenkomst. Bij internationale of digitale detachering zijn aanvullende afspraken nodig over toegang tot systemen, databeveiliging, intellectueel eigendom, compliance en communicatie.
Een detacheringsbrief aan de medewerker beschrijft doorgaans de opdracht, de duur, de rol, de rapportagelijn, de afspraken over werken op afstand en de relevante arbeidsvoorwaarden.
WorldEmp als allround detacheringspartner
WorldEmp is geen traditioneel uitzendbureau en geen partij die projecten overneemt. Wij leveren dedicated remote professionals die jouw team versterken.
Dat betekent dat jij de regie houdt over het werk. Jouw organisatie bepaalt prioriteiten, werkwijze, planning en kwaliteit. De professional werkt als onderdeel van jouw team.

Wij ondersteunen bij selectie, internationale verbinding, onboarding, begeleiding en continuïteit. Zo ontstaat een model dat verder gaat dan kortdurende inhuur en tegelijk flexibeler blijft dan volledig lokaal werven.

WorldEmp is relevant voor organisaties die structureel capaciteit nodig hebben in rollen als engineering, softwareontwikkeling, data, document control, planning, werkvoorbereiding en projectondersteuning.
De kracht zit in de combinatie van mensen, proces en internationale toegang tot talent. Niet harder zoeken in dezelfde krappe markt, maar capaciteit slimmer organiseren.

Veelvoorkomende vormen van detachering zijn detachering tussen afdelingen, externe detachering, internationale detachering, detachering bij non-profitorganisaties, detachering bij de opdrachtgever en digitale detachering.
Wat is een voorbeeld van detachering?

Een engineer is verbonden aan een detacheringsbureau en werkt twaalf maanden in het engineeringteam van een opdrachtgever. De opdrachtgever stuurt het werk aan. Het bureau verzorgt selectie, begeleiding en de contractuele afspraken.
Wat is internationale detachering?

Internationale detachering betekent dat een medewerker of professional werkt voor een vestiging, opdrachtgever of partnerorganisatie in het buitenland. Dat kan fysiek in het buitenland of digitaal vanaf afstand.
Wat is het voordeel van internationale detachering?

Het belangrijkste voordeel van internationale detachering is toegang tot internationale kennis en capaciteit. Voor bedrijven vergroot het de beschikbare talentpool. Voor professionals biedt het internationale ervaring zonder altijd te hoeven verhuizen.
Wat zegt de wet over detachering?

In Nederland is de Waadi de belangrijkste wet voor detachering. Die gaat over registratie, gelijke behandeling en het belemmeringsverbod. Ook cao-bepalingen, de Arbeidstijdenwet en fiscale regels kunnen van toepassing zijn.
Wat betekent ‘detacheren’?

Detacheren betekent iemand tijdelijk toewijzen aan een andere afdeling, organisatie of opdrachtgever. Iemand die gedetacheerd is, werkt dus elders, terwijl het dienstverband of de contractuele relatie bij een andere partij blijft.
Hoe lang duurt een detachering?
De duur van een detachering verschilt per opdracht. Het kan om enkele maanden gaan, maar ook om meerdere jaren. Bij WorldEmp ligt de nadruk op langdurige samenwerking en structurele teamuitbreiding.
Wat hoort er in een detacheringsbrief te staan?

Een detacheringsbrief bevat doorgaans de rol, de opdracht, de duur, de werktijden, de rapportagelijn, de locatie of afspraken over werken op afstand, de arbeidsvoorwaarden, geheimhouding en contactpersonen.
Wat is een detacheringsovereenkomst?
Een detacheringsovereenkomst is de overeenkomst waarin de detachering wordt vastgelegd. Die gaat doorgaans over rol, duur, kosten, verantwoordelijkheden, compliance en beëindiging.
Wat is een detacheringscontract in Nederland?

Een detacheringscontract in Nederland moet passen binnen het Nederlandse arbeidsrecht. Vaak wordt rekening gehouden met de Waadi-regels, cao-bepalingen, inlenersaansprakelijkheid, gelijke arbeidsvoorwaarden en de afspraken tussen uitlener en inlener.
Wat is een overeenkomst voor het detacheren van medewerkers?

Een overeenkomst voor het detacheren van medewerkers is het document dat het toewijzen van medewerkers aan een andere organisatie regelt. Daarin staan de praktische, juridische en financiële voorwaarden van de detachering.
Hoe is het om via een detacheringsbureau te werken?

Via een detacheringsbureau werken betekent dat een professional werkt voor een opdrachtgever terwijl het bureau de contractuele relatie of het dienstverband beheert. De opdrachtgever stuurt het dagelijkse werk aan, terwijl het bureau ondersteunt bij selectie, begeleiding en continuïteit.

Detachering is een praktische manier om kennis en capaciteit beschikbaar te maken wanneer organisaties die nodig hebben. Het werkt vooral goed wanneer de samenwerking helder is ingericht, de professional bij het team past en de opdrachtgever de regie over het werk houdt.

Bij WorldEmp combineren we detachering met een digitaal en internationaal model. Daarmee kunnen organisaties opschalen met dedicated remote professionals zonder de regie over werk, processen of kwaliteit te verliezen.
Voor bedrijven die blijven groeien in een krappe arbeidsmarkt is dit geen tijdelijke oplossing. Het is een slimmere manier om sterkere, flexibelere en toekomstbestendige teams te bouwen.

en.title: Solum Technology: drie jaar samenwerken met WorldEmp
en.description: A look back at three years of collaboration between Solum Technology and WorldEmp. On growth, specialist capacity, a sense of team and building a strong international team.

blocks.text: Solum Technology wanted to offer customers more than individual components. Delivering engineering and complete conveyor solutions as well called for extra specialist capacity. Working with WorldEmp, the company found a way to build that capacity with a team that genuinely became part of the organisation. We spoke about it with Martin de Koning, CEO of Solum Technology.
The step came out of scarcity in the Netherlands

For Solum the reason was clear. The specialist engineering knowledge they needed turned out to be barely available in the Netherlands. For De Koning, that was the moment to look beyond the usual routes.

“As a company we wanted to grow and offer customers the complete picture. For that you need people with the right engineering experience. They were simply not to be found for us in the Netherlands,” De Koning said.
Through WorldEmp, India came into view as a serious option. Not as a detached remote solution, but as a way to build a team purposefully that genuinely worked for Solum.

blocks.alt: offshore oil, gas, wind, jack-up, energy transition

blocks.text: ISO 42001 in practice: from engineering to data governance
Focused on quality from the start

What mattered to Solum was that the people in India worked full time and exclusively for the company. Only then, according to De Koning, can you really build commitment, responsibility and quality. The same went for the working environment. With their own Solum-branded office, the team got a clear place of its own, which mattered to Solum in building a sense of team and ownership.
“Dat moest echt wel bij ons team passen,” zei De Koning.
blocks.html: “Dat moest echt wel bij ons team passen,” zei De Koning.

blocks.text: What the partnership with WorldEmp gave him above all, he says, was the confidence that comes from having room to build carefully. First finding out whether it works professionally and personally, while at the same time genuinely investing in people who work for your organisation.

“That gave us the room to really find out whether it worked professionally and personally. At the same time, the people were genuinely working for Solum. So you are not building something temporary - from day one you are laying the foundations of your own team,” De Koning explained.
You build a team with attention

What became clear in the conversation with De Koning is that success does not only depend on finding the right people, but above all on how you shape the working relationship. You do not build a remote team by handing over work alone.
“A partnership like this asks for attention, time and involvement. You have to really bring people into your company, into your way of working and into where you want to go together,” said De Koning.

So from the start Solum chose frequent contact, clear alignment and an intensive onboarding. The first colleagues from India came to the Netherlands early on, and travelled to China as well. That, according to De Koning, is what made the difference. People got to know not only the work, but the company, the customers and each other.
Trust and ownership grow together

What stands out most in his account is how strongly De Koning approaches the partnership as one between equals. Not by fitting people to a Dutch standard, but by looking seriously at who they are, how they work and what they need in order to do well.

“You have to understand who you are working with. If you give people the room to take responsibility and you are open yourself, trust develops. And out of that trust, ownership grows,” De Koning said.

The approach paid off. Over the past few years the team in India has grown into a stable and committed group. Where a lot of day-to-day alignment was needed at first, the team now operates more and more independently and takes on more responsibility in delivery itself.
More than extra capacity
For Solum, working with WorldEmp has produced more than extra engineering capacity alone. It brought a strong team, more clout, and an organisation on firmer international footing.

It also became clear in the conversation that the process has given De Koning something personally. India brought him not only a team, but enjoyment in the work together. The energy, the positivity and the commitment of the team are what have stayed with him.
“They open the day with a smile and close the day with a smile. That enjoyment and that positivity are infectious. I have learned a great deal from it myself,” he said.

blocks.alt: WorldEmp

blocks.text: Interested? Want to know more?
Advice for companies considering this step

Asked what he would pass on to companies considering a comparable step, De Koning was clear. A choice like this asks for entrepreneurship and a willingness to genuinely invest in people. But that is exactly when it can deliver a great deal.
“Take the step. Give people a chance, make them a real part of your team and invest in the relationship. Do that well and you get an enormous amount back,” he concluded.

en.title: Solum Technology: drie jaar samenwerken met WorldEmp
en.description: A look back at three years of collaboration between Solum Technology and WorldEmp. On growth, specialist capacity, a sense of team and building a strong international team.

blocks.text: Solum Technology wanted to offer customers more than individual components. Delivering engineering and complete conveyor solutions as well called for extra specialist capacity. Working with WorldEmp, the company found a way to build that capacity with a team that genuinely became part of the organisation. We spoke about it with Martin de Koning, CEO of Solum Technology.
The step came out of scarcity in the Netherlands

For Solum the reason was clear. The specialist engineering knowledge they needed turned out to be barely available in the Netherlands. For De Koning, that was the moment to look beyond the usual routes.

“As a company we wanted to grow and offer customers the complete picture. For that you need people with the right engineering experience. They were simply not to be found for us in the Netherlands,” De Koning said.
Through WorldEmp, India came into view as a serious option. Not as a detached remote solution, but as a way to build a team purposefully that genuinely worked for Solum.

blocks.alt: offshore oil, gas, wind, jack-up, energy transition

blocks.text: ISO 42001 in practice: from engineering to data governance
Focused on quality from the start

What mattered to Solum was that the people in India worked full time and exclusively for the company. Only then, according to De Koning, can you really build commitment, responsibility and quality. The same went for the working environment. With their own Solum-branded office, the team got a clear place of its own, which mattered to Solum in building a sense of team and ownership.
“Dat moest echt wel bij ons team passen,” zei De Koning.
blocks.html: “Dat moest echt wel bij ons team passen,” zei De Koning.

blocks.text: What the partnership with WorldEmp gave him above all, he says, was the confidence that comes from having room to build carefully. First finding out whether it works professionally and personally, while at the same time genuinely investing in people who work for your organisation.

“That gave us the room to really find out whether it worked professionally and personally. At the same time, the people were genuinely working for Solum. So you are not building something temporary - from day one you are laying the foundations of your own team,” De Koning explained.
You build a team with attention

What became clear in the conversation with De Koning is that success does not only depend on finding the right people, but above all on how you shape the working relationship. You do not build a remote team by handing over work alone.
“A partnership like this asks for attention, time and involvement. You have to really bring people into your company, into your way of working and into where you want to go together,” said De Koning.

So from the start Solum chose frequent contact, clear alignment and an intensive onboarding. The first colleagues from India came to the Netherlands early on, and travelled to China as well. That, according to De Koning, is what made the difference. People got to know not only the work, but the company, the customers and each other.
Trust and ownership grow together

What stands out most in his account is how strongly De Koning approaches the partnership as one between equals. Not by fitting people to a Dutch standard, but by looking seriously at who they are, how they work and what they need in order to do well.

“You have to understand who you are working with. If you give people the room to take responsibility and you are open yourself, trust develops. And out of that trust, ownership grows,” De Koning said.

The approach paid off. Over the past few years the team in India has grown into a stable and committed group. Where a lot of day-to-day alignment was needed at first, the team now operates more and more independently and takes on more responsibility in delivery itself.
More than extra capacity
For Solum, working with WorldEmp has produced more than extra engineering capacity alone. It brought a strong team, more clout, and an organisation on firmer international footing.

It also became clear in the conversation that the process has given De Koning something personally. India brought him not only a team, but enjoyment in the work together. The energy, the positivity and the commitment of the team are what have stayed with him.
“They open the day with a smile and close the day with a smile. That enjoyment and that positivity are infectious. I have learned a great deal from it myself,” he said.

blocks.alt: WorldEmp

blocks.text: Interested? Want to know more?
Advice for companies considering this step

Asked what he would pass on to companies considering a comparable step, De Koning was clear. A choice like this asks for entrepreneurship and a willingness to genuinely invest in people. But that is exactly when it can deliver a great deal.
“Take the step. Give people a chance, make them a real part of your team and invest in the relationship. Do that well and you get an enormous amount back,” he concluded.
