nl.title: Sterkere semiconductorteams bouwen met internationaal talent
nl.description: Ontdek hoe semiconductorbedrijven internationaal talent kunnen inzetten om hun engineeringcapaciteit te versterken, tekorten op te vangen en duurzaam te groeien.

blocks.text: Deel drie van drie
De semiconductorindustrie heeft zich altijd ontwikkeld door grenzen te verleggen.
Kleinere componenten. Meer rekenkracht. Snellere verwerking. Geavanceerdere productie.

Vandaag ligt een van de knellendste beperkingen van de industrie echter niet in een laboratorium of cleanroom. Het is de groeiende afstand tussen wat semiconductorbedrijven willen bereiken en het gespecialiseerde talent dat daarvoor beschikbaar is.

In het eerste artikel van deze serie onderzochten we waarom talent een strategisch knelpunt is geworden. In het tweede keken we naar de gevolgen: langere recruitmentprocessen, hevige concurrentie om specialisten en toenemende druk op bestaande engineeringteams.
In dit laatste artikel kijken we naar wat er daarna komt.

Want semiconductorbedrijven kunnen niet wachten tot de arbeidsmarkt de vraag heeft ingehaald. Ze hebben een praktische manier nodig om toegang te krijgen tot gespecialiseerde expertise, hun teams te versterken en vooruit te blijven gaan — zonder in te leveren op samenwerking, kwaliteit of controle.

blocks.alt: offshore oil, gas, wind, jack-up, energy transition

blocks.text: Wanneer één vacature een hele roadmap beïnvloedt
Een moeilijk vervulbare vacature blijft zelden een geïsoleerd HR-vraagstuk.

Wanneer de juiste specialist niet gevonden kan worden, kunnen ontwikkelmijlpalen vertraging oplopen. Senior engineers besteden meer tijd aan het opvangen van capaciteitstekorten en minder tijd aan het oplossen van technische vraagstukken. Teams moeten projecten soms uitstellen of kansen laten liggen omdat de benodigde expertise ontbreekt.
Eén lege stoel kan een hele roadmap beïnvloeden.
De eerste reactie is vaak om de recruitmentinspanningen op te voeren: de vacature breder uitzetten, meer kandidaten benaderen en wachten tot het juiste profiel zich aandient.
Maar wat als het probleem niet ligt bij het bereik van de zoektocht?
Wat als de benodigde expertise simpelweg onvoldoende beschikbaar is op de lokale arbeidsmarkt?
Op dat punt is harder zoeken niet langer genoeg. Organisaties moeten anders gaan zoeken.
Het antwoord is misschien dichterbij dan de afstand doet vermoeden
Ergens in India werkt misschien een engineer met precies de expertise waar jouw organisatie naar op zoek is.
De uitdaging is om die persoon te vinden, te bepalen of hij of zij binnen jouw organisatie tot zijn recht komt en de voorwaarden te scheppen om echt onderdeel van jouw team te worden.
Daar komt WorldEmp in beeld.
WorldEmp verbindt Europese bedrijven met zorgvuldig geselecteerde professionals in India. Maar onze dienstverlening draait niet om het doorsturen van cv's of het zo snel mogelijk vullen van stoelen.
Wij slaan de brug tussen beschikbaar talent en de dagelijkse praktijk.

We beginnen met het begrijpen van de behoefte achter de functieomschrijving. Naast technische expertise beoordelen we communicatie, eigenaarschap, zelfstandigheid en culturele aansluiting. Vervolgens verzorgen we de lokale arbeidsrechtelijke structuur en blijven we de samenwerking ondersteunen nadat de nieuwe collega is gestart.

Het resultaat is geen losstaande externe kracht. Het is een dedicated professional die rechtstreeks samenwerkt met het team van de opdrachtgever, terwijl WorldEmp alles rond het werkgeverschap regelt.
Andere locatie. Eén team. Gedeelde doelen.
Hoe WorldEmp internationaal talent omzet in teamcapaciteit
Onze aanpak is opgebouwd rond vier samenhangende stappen: definiëren, selecteren, integreren en ondersteunen.
Elke stap is erop gericht onzekerheid te verkleinen en internationale recruitment om te zetten in een stabiele samenwerking voor de lange termijn.
Bepaal wat het team écht nodig heeft
Een functietitel vertelt zelden het hele verhaal.
Twee functies met dezelfde titel kunnen een totaal andere technische achtergrond, mate van zelfstandigheid en ervaring binnen gespecialiseerde engineeringomgevingen vragen.
WorldEmp begint daarom met een uitgebreide intake. Samen kijken we naar de doelstellingen van de organisatie, de technische omgeving, de teamsamenstelling en de huidige capaciteitsknelpunten.
Vragen die we samen beantwoorden

items: Welke expertise ontbreekt op dit moment binnen het team?
Wat moet de nieuwe collega kunnen opleveren?
Met welke systemen, tools en processen gaat hij of zij werken?
Hoe zelfstandig moet de professional kunnen werken?
Wanneer is de samenwerking na zes of twaalf maanden geslaagd?

blocks.text: Zo hebben we meer dan een vacature om in te vullen. Er ontstaat een helder beeld van de collega die de organisatie daadwerkelijk nodig heeft.
Selecteer op meer dan technische vaardigheden
Toegang tot een grote talentmarkt levert alleen waarde op wanneer het selectieproces nauwkeurig is.

WorldEmp werft kandidaten via het eigen netwerk in India en beoordeelt hen met een gestructureerd assessmentproces. Afhankelijk van de rol kan dat bestaan uit een screening op ervaring, technische toetsen, competentiegerichte interviews, STAR-interviews en TMA-assessments.
Technische kennis is essentieel, maar op zichzelf niet voldoende.

We kijken ook of de kandidaat complexe informatie helder kan overbrengen, zelfstandig kan werken terwijl hij of zij verbonden blijft met het team, verantwoordelijkheid neemt en goed omgaat met feedback en veranderende prioriteiten.

De opdrachtgever blijft betrokken bij de laatste interview- en selectierondes. WorldEmp geeft toegang, voert de assessments uit en presenteert een gerichte selectie. Het bedrijf beslist wie onderdeel wordt van het team.
Geen stapel cv's. Een zorgvuldig geselecteerde groep mensen die daadwerkelijk binnen de organisatie zou passen.
Integreer een collega — geen externe kracht
De juiste persoon vinden is slechts de helft van het werk.
De volgende stap is ervoor zorgen dat de professional ook over landsgrenzen heen effectief kan bijdragen.

Na de selectie ondersteunt WorldEmp de onboarding en helpt de specialist vertrouwd te raken met de systemen, processen en verwachtingen van de opdrachtgever. De professional werkt vanaf een WorldEmp-werklocatie in India en werkt rechtstreeks samen met collega's in Europa.
Hij of zij neemt deel aan overleggen, werkt mee aan gezamenlijke deliverables en raakt vertrouwd met de technische standaarden, documentatie en werkwijzen van de organisatie.

Die integratie is in de semiconductorindustrie extra belangrijk. Complex engineeringwerk vraagt om context, continuïteit en nauwe samenwerking tussen mensen die begrijpen hoe hun verantwoordelijkheden bijdragen aan het bredere product of systeem.
Een remote collega hoort niet buiten het team te staan wachten op instructies.
Die collega hoort onderdeel te zijn van het gesprek.
Wij regelen alles rondom het werk
Internationale samenwerking brengt praktische verantwoordelijkheden met zich mee.
Wie is lokaal de werkgever? Wie regelt contracten, salarisadministratie en HR? Waar werkt de professional? Wie ondersteunt de prestaties en lost uitdagingen op na de onboarding?
WorldEmp verzorgt die basis.

De opdrachtgever stuurt het technische werk, de prioriteiten en de dagelijkse verantwoordelijkheden van de specialist aan. WorldEmp verzorgt het lokale werkgeverschap, de salarisadministratie, HR-ondersteuning, werkplekfaciliteiten, performance management en de relevante complianceprocessen.

Gedurende de hele samenwerking blijven we in contact met zowel het bedrijf als de medewerker. Regelmatig overleg helpt om aandachtspunten vroeg te signaleren, professionele ontwikkeling te ondersteunen en de samenwerking stabiel te houden.
Zo kan de opdrachtgever zich richten op waarvoor de specialist is aangenomen: expertise inbrengen, innovatie ondersteunen en het team versterken.
Begin met de capaciteit die je vandaag nodig hebt
Niet iedere organisatie heeft meteen een groot internationaal team nodig.

Het vertrekpunt kan één specialist zijn wiens expertise lokaal moeilijk te vinden was. Het kan een kleine groep zijn die een nieuw programma ondersteunt, of extra capaciteit voor een engineeringteam dat tegen zijn grenzen aanloopt.

Via het Digital Knowledge Migrant-model van WorldEmp kunnen bedrijven dedicated professionals in India toevoegen aan hun bestaande teams. Wanneer meer flexibiliteit nodig is, kan detachering toegang geven tot specifieke kennis of extra capaciteit.
De samenwerking kan meegroeien met de behoefte.
Wat begint met één zorgvuldig geselecteerde professional kan uitgroeien tot een verbonden team dat kennis vasthoudt, continuïteit ondersteunt en ruimte maakt voor ambitieuzer werk.
Het doel is niet groei om de groei. Het gaat erom bedrijven de capaciteit te geven om door te gaan wanneer de lokale arbeidsmarkt hen zegt te wachten.
Technologie schept mogelijkheden. Mensen maken er vooruitgang van.
Door deze driedelige serie heen is één conclusie steeds duidelijker geworden.
De ambities van de semiconductorindustrie versnellen, maar ambitie zonder de mensen om die uit te voeren wordt uiteindelijk vertraging.

Fabrieken kunnen worden uitgebreid. Apparatuur kan worden geïnstalleerd. Investeringen kunnen worden goedgekeurd. Maar geen daarvan levert vooruitgang op zonder engineers en specialisten die technologie kunnen omzetten in betrouwbare oplossingen.
Het volgende concurrentievoordeel is daarom misschien menselijker dan technologisch: het vermogen om de juiste expertise te verbinden met de juiste organisatie, waar die expertise zich ook bevindt.
WorldEmp maakt die verbinding praktisch uitvoerbaar.
Laten we elkaar spreken op SEMICON India 2026
SEMICON India 2026 vindt plaats van 17 tot en met 19 september 2026 in Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, en brengt organisaties uit het wereldwijde semiconductor- en elektronica-ecosysteem samen.
Frank Korf, Noortje van Sambeek en Chris van der Deijl vertegenwoordigen WorldEmp op dit toonaangevende internationale semiconductor-evenement.
Je vindt ons in het NL Pavilion, waar WorldEmp samen met High Tech NL Semiconductors aanwezig is.

Het evenement staat vol gesprekken over investeringen, productie, innovatie en groei. Wij willen ruimte maken voor een ander belangrijk gesprek — over de mensen die nodig zijn om die ambities mogelijk te maken.

“De toekomst van de semiconductorindustrie wordt bepaald door de verbindingen die we vandaag leggen. Ik kijk ernaar uit om mensen te ontmoeten, ideeën uit te wisselen en mee te bouwen aan wat er komt.”
Frank Korf, CEO en oprichter

“De vaart in de Indiase semiconductorindustrie is niet te negeren. Ik kijk ernaar uit om wereldwijde ambitie te verbinden met Indiase expertise — en partnerships op te bouwen die de industrie vooruithelpen.”
Noortje van Sambeek, Strategic Lead Partner
“SEMICON India is de plek waar grote ambities en echte kansen samenkomen. Ik kijk ernaar uit om te ontdekken hoe de juiste mensen en partnerships die ambities kunnen omzetten in blijvende groei.”
Chris van der Deijl, Marketing Director
Op 18 september 2026 om 08.30 uur organiseren WorldEmp en NXL een exclusief ontbijt bij Vivanta New Delhi, Dwarka.

Samen met leiders uit de industrie bespreken we wat er nodig is om in India op te bouwen en op te schalen — van het vinden van gespecialiseerde professionals tot het creëren van de teamcapaciteit die duurzame groei vraagt.

Staat een cruciale functie al te lang open, heeft jouw engineeringteam ruimte nodig om te groeien of wil je ontdekken hoe talent uit India jouw organisatie kan versterken? Neem die uitdaging dan mee naar de gesprekstafel.
Ontmoet Frank, Noortje en Chris bij het NL Pavilion — of schuif bij ons aan tijdens het ontbijt.
Laten we praten over de talentuitdaging achter jouw ambities — en over de mensen die die vooruit kunnen brengen.

en.title: The Reality of the Semiconductor Industry: Talent as the New Bottleneck
en.description: Discover why specialized talent has become the semiconductor industry's biggest bottleneck and how organizations can build resilient teams to drive innovation and long-term growth.

blocks.text: Building Workforce Resilience for Sustainable Growth in the Semiconductor Industry
blocks.html: Building Workforce Resilience for Sustainable Growth in the Semiconductor Industry

blocks.text: For decades, the semiconductor industry has been characterized by its continual advancement beyond established technological boundaries. Progress has been marked by the development of smaller geometries, faster processors, higher yields, and more powerful systems enabled by increasingly sophisticated technologies. Each generation of innovation has been accompanied by predictions of technical limitations, yet the industry has consistently redefined what is considered achievable.

Progress has been marked by the development of smaller geometries, faster processors, higher yields, and more powerful systems enabled by increasingly sophisticated technologies. Each generation of innovation has been accompanied by predictions of technical limitations, yet the industry has consistently redefined what is considered achievable.

blocks.text: However, the next significant limitation facing the sector may not arise from engineering complexity, manufacturing constraints, or supply chain dependencies. Instead, it may originate from factors that are less immediately visible. Human capital.

blocks.text: As demand for semiconductors accelerates across artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, electrification, and digital infrastructure, access to specialized expertise is emerging as a critical industry constraint. For many organizations, discussions are shifting beyond technology roadmaps and production targets.

A central question is whether the industry can develop the expertise necessary to support its projected growth. Additionally, it remains to be seen whether Europe’s semiconductor ecosystem can scale at the pace required by global demand.

blocks.text: Semiconductors Have Become Strategic Infrastructure

Few industries have undergone such a rapid transformation in strategic importance as the semiconductor sector. What was once considered a specialised component industry now sits at the centre of global economic growth, industrial competitiveness and technological sovereignty.

blocks.text: Artificial intelligence models require increasingly powerful compute infrastructure.

blocks.text: Modern vehicles increasingly rely on hundreds to thousands of semiconductor devices supporting everything from battery management systems to advanced driver assistance technologies. Factories are becoming more autonomous, connected and intelligent. Healthcare technologies continue to integrate sensors, processing capabilities and embedded systems into devices that were previously mechanical.

blocks.text: Industry forecasts from organisations including McKinsey, Deloitte and other market analysts continue to project that global semiconductor revenues could exceed US$1 trillion before the end of the decade, driven by simultaneous growth across multiple sectors rather than reliance on a single technology cycle. This distinction is significant.

blocks.text: The Netherlands Sits at the Heart of This Transformation

Within Europe, the Netherlands holds a distinctive position in the global semiconductor value chain. Unlike many countries that focus primarily on chip fabrication, the Netherlands has established an international reputation for its technologies, equipment, and engineering expertise that facilitate advanced semiconductor manufacturing worldwide.
blocks.html: Within Europe, the Netherlands holds a distinctive position in the global semiconductor value chain. Unlike many countries that focus primarily on chip fabrication, the Netherlands has established an international reputation for its technologies, equipment, and engineering expertise that facilitate advanced semiconductor manufacturing worldwide.

blocks.text: Over the past decades, close collaboration between industry, universities and government has created one of Europe’s strongest semiconductor ecosystems. Regions such as Eindhoven, Delft, Twente and Nijmegen have grown into internationally recognised centres for innovation, bringing together manufacturers, suppliers, research institutions and highly specialised engineering talent.

As global demand increases, the primary challenge extends beyond maintaining technological leadership to ensuring the ecosystem possesses the expertise required for its next phase of growth.

blocks.text: Growth Creates New Questions

Historically, discussions about growth in the semiconductor industry have centred on manufacturing capacity, investment cycles and supply chain resilience. Those conversations remain highly relevant. However, the industry's next phase of growth introduces another variable that is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore: expertise.
blocks.html: Historically, discussions about growth in the semiconductor industry have centred on manufacturing capacity, investment cycles and supply chain resilience. Those conversations remain highly relevant. However, the industry's next phase of growth introduces another variable that is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore: expertise.

blocks.text: As semiconductor technologies become more sophisticated, the knowledge required to design, manufacture and optimise them becomes increasingly specialised. At the same time, engineering disciplines that once operated independently are becoming more interconnected. Software and hardware development continue to converge, while data analytics, automation, and AI play an increasingly important role in modern semiconductor manufacturing environments.

Software and hardware development continue to converge, while data analytics, automation, and AI play an increasingly important role in modern semiconductor manufacturing environments.

blocks.text: As a result, product development and production processes are becoming more complex, increasing the demand for highly specialised engineering capabilities across the value chain.
blocks.html: As a result, product development and production processes are becoming more complex, increasing the demand for highly specialised engineering capabilities across the value chain.

blocks.text: The implications are significant. Manufacturing capacity can be expanded. New equipment can be purchased. Facilities can be built. Developing experienced semiconductor expertise, however, follows a very different timeline. It is a long-term investment that depends on education, hands-on experience and continuous knowledge development.

blocks.text: The Talent Equation Is Changing
Semiconductor organisations have always depended on highly specialised knowledge. What is changing is the pace at which demand for that expertise is growing.
blocks.html: Semiconductor organisations have always depended on highly specialised knowledge. What is changing is the pace at which demand for that expertise is growing.

blocks.text: The rise of artificial intelligence, advanced packaging, next-generation mobility and industrial digitalisation is creating demand for capabilities that often take years to develop. Many technical disciplines within the semiconductor industry rely not only on formal education, but also on hands-on experience gained in highly complex design and manufacturing environments.

blocks.text: This makes expertise fundamentally different from other forms of industrial capacity. While organisations can invest in new equipment, facilities and technology, investment alone cannot instantly create experienced semiconductor specialists. Expertise is built over time through practical experience, collaboration and continuous learning.

Expertise is built over time through practical experience, collaboration and continuous learning.

blocks.text: For organisations operating in fast-moving markets, this raises an increasingly important strategic question: How do you scale innovation when the expertise required to support it develops more slowly than the market itself?

blocks.text: The Dutch Labour Market Adds Another Layer of Complexity

The Netherlands has long benefited from a highly educated workforce and a strong international reputation in engineering and technology. At the same time, technical labour shortages are becoming increasingly visible across multiple sectors, with the semiconductor industry feeling these pressures particularly strongly due to the specialised nature of many roles.
blocks.html: The Netherlands has long benefited from a highly educated workforce and a strong international reputation in engineering and technology. At the same time, technical labour shortages are becoming increasingly visible across multiple sectors, with the semiconductor industry feeling these pressures particularly strongly due to the specialised nature of many roles.

blocks.text: The Brainport region provides perhaps the clearest example. As one of Europe's leading high-tech ecosystems, it continues to attract investment, expansion projects and international attention. However, this success also creates new challenges. Growing organisations are competing for the same specialist expertise; supplier networks face increasing pressure; and, in several disciplines, demand for experienced engineering talent is outpacing the development of local talent pipelines.

blocks.text: This challenge is not unique to the Netherlands. However, for a country that plays such a critical role in Europe's semiconductor ambitions, ensuring a sustainable pipeline of specialised talent has become an increasingly important strategic consideration.

blocks.text: A Different Kind of Strategic Discussion
Traditionally, workforce discussions have focused on recruitment, retention and training. While these remain important, the semiconductor industry increasingly requires a broader perspective.
blocks.html: Traditionally, workforce discussions have focused on recruitment, retention and training. While these remain important, the semiconductor industry increasingly requires a broader perspective.

blocks.text: When access to expertise begins to influence investment decisions, expansion plans and innovation timelines, workforce planning becomes more than an operational function—it becomes a strategic business priority. Questions about engineering capability are now closely linked to competitiveness, resilience and long-term growth.

blocks.text: For leadership teams, this represents an important shift. The challenge is no longer simply about filling vacancies. It is about ensuring sustained access to the expertise needed to support innovation, maintain competitiveness and enable long-term growth.

blocks.text: The Beginning of a Larger Industry Conversation

Throughout its history, the semiconductor industry has consistently overcome extraordinary technical challenges, pushing the boundaries of what is possible through innovation, engineering excellence and continuous investment.

blocks.text: The next challenge, however, may be different. It is not simply about developing more advanced technologies or expanding manufacturing capacity, but about ensuring the industry has access to the specialised expertise needed to sustain that progress.

blocks.text: Nederland staat centraal in deze transformatie

Binnen Europa neemt Nederland een unieke positie in binnen de wereldwijde semiconductorwaardeketen. In tegenstelling tot veel andere landen, die zich voornamelijk richten op de productie van chips, heeft Nederland een internationale reputatie opgebouwd dankzij de technologieën, apparatuur en engineeringexpertise die wereldwijd geavanceerde semiconductorproductie mogelijk maken.

blocks.text: Door de nauwe samenwerking tussen het bedrijfsleven, kennisinstellingen en de overheid is de afgelopen decennia een van de sterkste semiconductor-ecosystemen van Europa ontstaan. Regio's zoals Eindhoven, Delft, Twente en Nijmegen zijn uitgegroeid tot internationaal erkende innovatiehubs waar fabrikanten, toeleveranciers, onderzoeksinstellingen en hooggespecialiseerde engineeringprofessionals samenkomen.

blocks.text: Groei brengt nieuwe vraagstukken met zich mee

Traditioneel draaiden gesprekken over groei in de semiconductorindustrie vooral om productiecapaciteit, investeringscycli en de veerkracht van de toeleveringsketen. Die onderwerpen blijven onverminderd belangrijk. Tegelijkertijd brengt de volgende groeifase van de sector een nieuwe uitdaging met zich mee die steeds moeilijker te negeren is: gespecialiseerde expertise.

blocks.text: Naarmate semiconductortechnologie steeds geavanceerder wordt, neemt ook de kennis toe die nodig is om deze technologieën te ontwerpen, produceren en optimaliseren. Daarnaast groeien engineeringdisciplines die voorheen los van elkaar opereerden steeds verder naar elkaar toe. Software- en hardwareontwikkeling raken steeds sterker met elkaar verweven, terwijl data-analyse, automatisering en kunstmatige intelligentie een steeds belangrijkere rol spelen binnen moderne semiconductorproductie.

blocks.text: De talentvergelijking verandert
Semiconductororganisaties zijn altijd afhankelijk geweest van hooggespecialiseerde kennis. Wat verandert, is de snelheid waarmee de vraag naar die expertise groeit.

blocks.text: De opkomst van kunstmatige intelligentie, advanced packaging, next-generation mobility en industriële digitalisering zorgt voor een groeiende vraag naar vaardigheden die vaak jaren kosten om te ontwikkelen. Veel technische disciplines binnen de semiconductorindustrie zijn niet alleen gebaseerd op formeel onderwijs, maar ook op praktijkervaring die wordt opgedaan in complexe ontwerp- en productieomgevingen.

blocks.text: De Nederlandse arbeidsmarkt voegt een extra uitdaging toe

Nederland beschikt al jarenlang over een hoogopgeleide beroepsbevolking en een sterke internationale reputatie op het gebied van engineering en technologie. Tegelijkertijd worden de tekorten aan technisch talent in verschillende sectoren steeds zichtbaarder. Binnen de semiconductorindustrie zijn deze uitdagingen extra groot, doordat veel functies een zeer gespecialiseerde expertise vereisen.

en.description: Discover why specialised talent has become the new bottleneck in the semiconductor industry and how organisations are building sustainable growth and innovation.

blocks.text: Part Two of Three
blocks.html: Part Two of Three

blocks.text: In the first article of this series, we explored how access to specialised expertise is becoming one of the semiconductor industry's most important strategic considerations. As investment accelerates across artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, automotive technology and digital infrastructure, the conversation has evolved beyond manufacturing capacity and technology leadership. Increasingly, it is about people.

blocks.text: Today, that challenge is no longer theoretical.

blocks.text: Across the Dutch and European semiconductor ecosystem, organisations are experiencing the operational consequences of a workforce that cannot expand as quickly as the industry itself. Hiring cycles are becoming longer, experienced engineers are increasingly difficult to attract, and technical knowledge is becoming concentrated within a limited number of specialists.

blocks.text: Demand for Talent Is Growing Faster Than Supply
Few countries illustrate this challenge more clearly than the Netherlands.
blocks.html: Few countries illustrate this challenge more clearly than the Netherlands.

blocks.text: The Dutch semiconductor ecosystem continues to attract investment, supported by globally recognised innovation hubs such as Brainport Eindhoven and a strong collaboration between industry, academia and government. Yet success has also intensified competition for highly specialised talent.
blocks.html: The Dutch semiconductor ecosystem continues to attract investment, supported by globally recognised innovation hubs such as Brainport Eindhoven and a strong collaboration between industry, academia and government. Yet success has also intensified competition for highly specialised talent.

blocks.text: According to Brainport Eindhoven, the Netherlands is expected to require approximately 38,000 additional semiconductor professionals over the next five years, while the Brainport region alone anticipates around 26,000 vacancies across the semiconductor value chain. These figures reflect not only industry growth but also the increasing complexity of semiconductor technologies and the skills required to support them.

These figures reflect not only industry growth but also the increasing complexity of semiconductor technologies and the skills required to support them.

blocks.text: Professor Maarten Steinbuch, Scientific Director of the Eindhoven AI Systems Institute and one of the Netherlands' leading voices on technology and innovation, has repeatedly emphasised that talent has become one of the defining challenges for the sector. Discussing initiatives such as Project Beethoven, he noted that although significant investments are being made to strengthen the Dutch talent pipeline, demand continues to outpace supply.

Discussing initiatives such as Project Beethoven, he noted that although significant investments are being made to strengthen the Dutch talent pipeline, demand continues to outpace supply.

blocks.text: The challenge, therefore, is not a lack of ambition. It is the simple reality that developing experienced semiconductor professionals takes time.
blocks.html: The challenge, therefore, is not a lack of ambition. It is the simple reality that developing experienced semiconductor professionals takes time.

blocks.text: Unlike manufacturing capacity, expertise cannot be scaled overnight.
blocks.html: Unlike manufacturing capacity, expertise cannot be scaled overnight.

blocks.text: The Cost of Searching for Too Long
Long hiring cycles have become an accepted reality across much of the semiconductor industry. However, the true cost often extends far beyond an unfilled vacancy.
blocks.html: Long hiring cycles have become an accepted reality across much of the semiconductor industry. However, the true cost often extends far beyond an unfilled vacancy.

blocks.text: When organisations spend months searching for highly specialised engineers, project milestones can shift, product development slows and existing engineering teams absorb additional responsibilities. Senior specialists frequently divide their time between technical work, mentoring colleagues, interviewing candidates and maintaining increasingly complex development environments.
blocks.html: When organisations spend months searching for highly specialised engineers, project milestones can shift, product development slows and existing engineering teams absorb additional responsibilities. Senior specialists frequently divide their time between technical work, mentoring colleagues, interviewing candidates and maintaining increasingly complex development environments.

blocks.text: Over time, these pressures influence more than productivity.
blocks.html: Over time, these pressures influence more than productivity.

blocks.text: They affect an organisation's ability to innovate.
blocks.html: They affect an organisation's ability to innovate.

blocks.text: Deloitte's 2025 Global Semiconductor Industry Outlook identifies workforce availability as one of the industry's most significant long-term business challenges, noting that attracting, developing and retaining skilled professionals has become increasingly critical as advanced technologies continue to evolve.
blocks.html: Deloitte's 2025 Global Semiconductor Industry Outlook identifies workforce availability as one of the industry's most significant long-term business challenges, noting that attracting, developing and retaining skilled professionals has become increasingly critical as advanced technologies continue to evolve.

blocks.text: For leadership teams, workforce planning is no longer simply an operational responsibility. It has become a strategic capability.
blocks.html: For leadership teams, workforce planning is no longer simply an operational responsibility. It has become a strategic capability.

blocks.text: When Specialist Knowledge Disappears
Another workforce challenge receives considerably less attention.
blocks.html: Another workforce challenge receives considerably less attention.

blocks.text: Many semiconductor organisations rely on a relatively small number of engineers who possess years of accumulated technical knowledge. Whether working in verification, physical design, process integration, packaging or manufacturing optimisation, these specialists often carry expertise that extends well beyond documented processes.
blocks.html: Many semiconductor organisations rely on a relatively small number of engineers who possess years of accumulated technical knowledge. Whether working in verification, physical design, process integration, packaging or manufacturing optimisation, these specialists often carry expertise that extends well beyond documented processes.

blocks.text: When experienced professionals retire, relocate or pursue new opportunities, organisations lose more than headcount.
blocks.html: When experienced professionals retire, relocate or pursue new opportunities, organisations lose more than headcount.

blocks.text: They lose context.
blocks.html: They lose context.

blocks.text: They lose practical knowledge developed through years of product development, customer collaboration and manufacturing experience.
blocks.html: They lose practical knowledge developed through years of product development, customer collaboration and manufacturing experience.

blocks.text: As semiconductor technologies become increasingly sophisticated, preserving this institutional knowledge is becoming just as important as recruiting new talent.
blocks.html: As semiconductor technologies become increasingly sophisticated, preserving this institutional knowledge is becoming just as important as recruiting new talent.

blocks.text: The workforce discussion is therefore expanding.
blocks.html: The workforce discussion is therefore expanding.

blocks.text: It is no longer only about attracting engineers, but also about ensuring knowledge continuity across the organisation.
blocks.html: It is no longer only about attracting engineers, but also about ensuring knowledge continuity across the organisation.

blocks.text: The Battle for Talent Is Global
The semiconductor labour market has also become significantly more international.
blocks.html: The semiconductor labour market has also become significantly more international.

blocks.text: Dutch organisations are no longer competing solely with neighbouring companies in Eindhoven, Delft or Nijmegen. The same engineers are increasingly being approached by employers across Germany, Ireland, the United States, Taiwan, Singapore and other rapidly expanding semiconductor markets.
blocks.html: Dutch organisations are no longer competing solely with neighbouring companies in Eindhoven, Delft or Nijmegen. The same engineers are increasingly being approached by employers across Germany, Ireland, the United States, Taiwan, Singapore and other rapidly expanding semiconductor markets.

blocks.text: At the same time, governments around the world continue investing heavily in domestic semiconductor ecosystems, further increasing demand for experienced professionals.
blocks.html: At the same time, governments around the world continue investing heavily in domestic semiconductor ecosystems, further increasing demand for experienced professionals.

blocks.text: This creates a structural challenge.
blocks.html: This creates a structural challenge.

blocks.text: The pool of highly specialised semiconductor engineers is growing, but demand is growing even faster.
blocks.html: The pool of highly specialised semiconductor engineers is growing, but demand is growing even faster.

blocks.text: As Maarten Steinbuch observed during his discussion with WorldEmp, "Businesses want to move forward, to innovate, but that's not possible if you lack the people. And if you're not progressing, you're falling behind in the global market."
blocks.html: As Maarten Steinbuch observed during his discussion with WorldEmp, "Businesses want to move forward, to innovate, but that's not possible if you lack the people. And if you're not progressing, you're falling behind in the global market."

blocks.text: His observation captures a broader shift taking place across the industry. Access to expertise is becoming directly linked to competitiveness.
blocks.html: His observation captures a broader shift taking place across the industry. Access to expertise is becoming directly linked to competitiveness.

blocks.text: The Demand for Expertise Is Changing
These developments are encouraging semiconductor organisations to rethink how engineering capability is built.
blocks.html: These developments are encouraging semiconductor organisations to rethink how engineering capability is built.

blocks.text: Traditional recruitment remains essential, but increasingly it is complemented by broader workforce strategies. International collaboration, distributed engineering teams and globally connected R&D organisations are becoming more common across the semiconductor industry, enabling organisations to access specialised expertise while maintaining engineering quality and business continuity.
blocks.html: Traditional recruitment remains essential, but increasingly it is complemented by broader workforce strategies. International collaboration, distributed engineering teams and globally connected R&D organisations are becoming more common across the semiconductor industry, enabling organisations to access specialised expertise while maintaining engineering quality and business continuity.

blocks.text: This represents an important change in mindset.
blocks.html: This represents an important change in mindset.

blocks.text: Rather than asking where talent can be found, leadership teams are increasingly considering how expertise can remain continuously available throughout the lifecycle of increasingly complex technologies.
blocks.html: Rather than asking where talent can be found, leadership teams are increasingly considering how expertise can remain continuously available throughout the lifecycle of increasingly complex technologies.

blocks.text: The organisations best positioned for long-term growth may not simply be those that recruit the fastest.
blocks.html: The organisations best positioned for long-term growth may not simply be those that recruit the fastest.

blocks.text: They may be those that build the most resilient engineering ecosystems.
blocks.html: They may be those that build the most resilient engineering ecosystems.

blocks.text: Throughout its history, the semiconductor industry has repeatedly overcome technical barriers through innovation, collaboration and long-term investment.
blocks.html: Throughout its history, the semiconductor industry has repeatedly overcome technical barriers through innovation, collaboration and long-term investment.

blocks.text: The next challenge is different.
blocks.html: The next challenge is different.

blocks.text: It is ensuring that engineering capability grows alongside technological ambition.
blocks.html: It is ensuring that engineering capability grows alongside technological ambition.

blocks.text: As the industry continues expanding, workforce resilience will increasingly influence innovation capacity, operational continuity and competitive advantage. Organisations that treat access to specialised expertise as a strategic priority—not simply a recruitment objective—will be better positioned to sustain growth in an increasingly competitive global market. At WorldEmp, these conversations are becoming increasingly common among technology leaders across Europe. Through partnerships with companies building distributed engineering teams, we see a growing shift towards workforce models that combine local leadership with global expertise, enabling organisations to scale without compromising quality, continuity or control.

nl.title: De realiteit van de semiconductorindustrie: talent als bottleneck
nl.description: Ontdek waarom gespecialiseerd talent de nieuwe bottleneck wordt in de semiconductorindustrie en hoe organisaties bouwen aan duurzame groei en innovatie.

blocks.text: Deel twee van drie
blocks.html: Deel twee van drie

blocks.text: In het eerste artikel van deze serie onderzochten we hoe toegang tot gespecialiseerde expertise is uitgegroeid tot een van de belangrijkste strategische vraagstukken binnen de semiconductorindustrie. Nu de investeringen in kunstmatige intelligentie, geavanceerde productie, automotive technologie en digitale infrastructuur blijven toenemen, verschuift de discussie van productiecapaciteit en technologische innovatie naar een ander cruciaal onderwerp: mensen.

blocks.text: Die uitdaging is vandaag de dag niet langer theoretisch.
blocks.html: Die uitdaging is vandaag de dag niet langer theoretisch.

blocks.text: Binnen het Nederlandse en Europese semiconductor-ecosysteem ervaren organisaties steeds vaker de operationele gevolgen van een arbeidsmarkt die niet in hetzelfde tempo groeit als de sector zelf. Wervingstrajecten duren langer, ervaren engineers zijn steeds moeilijker te vinden en specialistische kennis raakt geconcentreerd bij een beperkte groep professionals.

blocks.text: De vraag naar talent groeit sneller dan het aanbod
Weinig landen illustreren deze uitdaging zo duidelijk als Nederland.
blocks.html: Weinig landen illustreren deze uitdaging zo duidelijk als Nederland.

blocks.text: Het Nederlandse semiconductor-ecosysteem blijft grote investeringen aantrekken, ondersteund door internationaal erkende innovatieclusters zoals Brainport Eindhoven en de sterke samenwerking tussen bedrijfsleven, kennisinstellingen en overheid. Juist dat succes heeft echter ook geleid tot een steeds intensere concurrentie om hooggespecialiseerd talent.
blocks.html: Het Nederlandse semiconductor-ecosysteem blijft grote investeringen aantrekken, ondersteund door internationaal erkende innovatieclusters zoals Brainport Eindhoven en de sterke samenwerking tussen bedrijfsleven, kennisinstellingen en overheid. Juist dat succes heeft echter ook geleid tot een steeds intensere concurrentie om hooggespecialiseerd talent.

blocks.text: Volgens Brainport Eindhoven heeft Nederland de komende vijf jaar ongeveer 38.000 extra semiconductorprofessionals nodig. Alleen al in de Brainport-regio worden circa 26.000 vacatures verwacht binnen de volledige semiconductorwaardeketen. Deze cijfers weerspiegelen niet alleen de groei van de sector, maar ook de toenemende complexiteit van semiconductortechnologieën en de specialistische vaardigheden die daarvoor nodig zijn.

Deze cijfers weerspiegelen niet alleen de groei van de sector, maar ook de toenemende complexiteit van semiconductortechnologieën en de specialistische vaardigheden die daarvoor nodig zijn.

blocks.text: Maarten Steinbuch, wetenschappelijk directeur van het Eindhoven AI Systems Institute en een van de meest vooraanstaande experts op het gebied van technologie en innovatie in Nederland, benadrukt al geruime tijd dat talent een van de grootste uitdagingen voor de sector is geworden. In gesprekken over initiatieven zoals Project Beethoven gaf hij aan dat er weliswaar fors wordt geïnvesteerd in het versterken van de Nederlandse talentpijplijn, maar dat de vraag nog altijd sneller groeit dan het aanbod.

en.title: What I learned in Shanghai and Seoul about the future of our high-tech and semiconductor industry
en.description: On my trip to Shanghai and SEMICON Korea I saw how fast the semiconductor industry is growing, and why dedicated remote teams are becoming crucial for Dutch high-tech companies

blocks.text: Blog: Frank Korf
blocks.html: Blog: Frank Korf

blocks.text: In the space of a few days I went from a pump factory in Shanghai to the show floor of SEMICON Korea in Seoul. Two trips, two countries, but with a clear common thread. Everywhere you feel the same pressure on speed, innovation and talent.

In Shanghai I stood in a factory hall where automation is thundering ahead. New production lines, smart robots, tightly organised processes. At the same time I noticed how open the conversations with my Chinese contacts were. They were about engineering, about working together, but also simply about what it is like to build a company at a time like this.

A few days later I was walking in Seoul between the stands of the big names in the global chip industry. We visited SK hynix and LG Electronics, and again the picture was clear. The industry is growing hard, the investments are enormous, and expectations of suppliers and partners are only rising.

blocks.alt: offshore oil, gas, wind, jack-up, energy transition

blocks.text: A Sustainable Alternative: Digital Knowledge Migrants

At WorldEmp, we believe there’s a smarter way. Our model focuses on digital knowledge migrants: highly educated international professionals who work for Dutch companies directly from their home countries, fully integrated into the team.

blocks.text: Remote teams as a fixed part of our future

This trip has confirmed my conviction that dedicated remote teams are becoming a lasting part of how we deliver high-tech and semiconductor projects in the Netherlands. Not as a quick trick, but as a considered, durable way to keep capacity and knowledge up to strength.

If you are wrestling with the same questions in your own organisation, I would invite you to talk about it openly. Not to sell you a solution straight away, but to explore together how we can organise talent and collaboration more intelligently. That, in the end, is what these trips are really about for me.

en.title: De energietransitie stokt door gebrek aan capaciteit
en.description: The energy transition asks for more than ambition. Find out why technical capacity is needed to accelerate green energy, electrification and grid expansion.

blocks.text: Door: Jan Joosten, Business Partner WorldEmp
blocks.html: Door: Jan Joosten, Business Partner WorldEmp

blocks.text: Iedereen wil vooruit

We all want to be less dependent on fossil energy. We want cleaner generation, reliable grids and an energy system that fits the next generation better. For companies, governments and citizens that is no longer an abstract goal. It is about affordable energy, security of supply and growing sustainably.

Behind every solar park, wind project, battery storage system or grid expansion programme there is therefore a wider promise. Not only to the immediate client, but to the customer behind them. A factory that wants to electrify. A logistics centre that needs charging infrastructure. A municipality that wants to meet its sustainability targets. An end user counting on green energy.
De ambitie is duidelijk. De uitvoering staat onder druk.

Much of that demand is replacement demand, driven by the expected outflow of around 118,000 employees in the same period. Techniek Nederland uses the same forecast to underline that the sector is facing a long term workforce challenge.

blocks.text: From labor shortage to capacity challenge

Many organizations still approach tight labor markets primarily as a recruitment issue. That is understandable, but incomplete. A vacancy that remains open for months is usually only the visible symptom. Beneath it lie increasing workload, backlogs in documentation, delays in preparation, fragmented data, and growing dependence on a small group of scarce senior specialists.

blocks.text: That distinction matters. A recruitment problem calls for more inflow. A capacity problem calls for a different way of organizing work. In engineering and industry, that second question has become more urgent because sustainability programs, digitalization, and infrastructure projects are increasing demand for technical capacity, while the labor market remains tight. In its Digital Decade Country Report, the European Commission also points to persistent shortages of ICT specialists and pressure on higher education in the Netherlands.

blocks.text: From that perspective, remote talent is most relevant as a structural addition to the existing team model. Not as a replacement for all local roles, but as a way to organize scarce capacity differently and more robustly.

blocks.text: 1. Remote talent expands the talent pool in a persistently tight market

The first reason is the most fundamental. As long as organizations search mainly locally or nationally, they compete with other employers in the same limited and overheated talent pool. In a market where UWV signals persistent labor shortages and the engineering sector must absorb both growth and replacement demand in the coming years, that makes organizations vulnerable.

blocks.text: 2. Remote talent makes organizations less dependent on local outflow and education dynamics

The second reason is more strategic. Organizations that rely almost entirely on one national labor market for structural capacity are also fully exposed to the outflow, ageing, and educational choices within that same market. The Wij Techniek forecast shows how heavily replacement demand will weigh in the coming years. At the same time, UWV underlines that labor market tightness remains persistent across virtually all regions.

blocks.text: That means the risk increases when organizations try to build their workforce exclusively through local hiring. Remote talent spreads that risk. It makes an organization less dependent on whether enough young technical professionals enter the labor market locally, whether experienced professionals remain available, or whether new skill sets are trained quickly enough. In that sense, remote capacity is not only an answer to today’s shortages, but also a way to make the workforce less vulnerable to tomorrow’s labor market pressures.

blocks.text: 3. Remote talent makes capacity scalable and continuous

A third reason is that remote talent fits a structural shortage better than a model that depends primarily on urgent temporary hiring, overtime, or internal task redistribution. Temporary solutions may ease pressure, but they rarely build lasting capacity. A structural model works differently: professionals who operate within the same processes, systems, and meeting structures over a longer period build knowledge of files, work rhythms, and standards. As a result, their effectiveness increases over time.

blocks.text: This also makes peak workloads easier to manage. In those situations, a fixed additional layer of capacity that is already onboarded is more valuable than having to scale up from scratch every time. Capacity then becomes not only larger, but also more stable and more predictable.

blocks.text: 4. Remote talent makes scarce senior expertise more productive

In many technical organizations, the bottleneck is not only the number of people available, but also how senior expertise is used. When engineers, project managers, and technical coordinators spend a large share of their time on revisions, documentation, reporting, checks, and preparatory work, pressure increases precisely on the people needed for design decisions, technical judgment, and risk management. Signals from the sector about the shortage of engineers make it clear how valuable that time has become.

When engineers, project managers, and technical coordinators spend a large share of their time on revisions, documentation, reporting, checks, and preparatory work, pressure increases precisely on the people needed for design decisions, technical judgment, and risk management. Signals from the sector about the shortage of engineers make it clear how valuable that time has become.

blocks.text: Remote talent can help break that pattern by structurally supporting execution focused and process oriented activities. That allows senior time to shift back toward the work where it adds the greatest value. In a market where experienced technical professionals remain scarce, this is not a marginal optimization issue, but a core component of capacity policy.

blocks.text: 5. Remote talent strengthens the foundation under quality, documentation, and compliance

In engineering and industry, a capacity problem often becomes most visible in the work that gets postponed. As built documentation falls behind, data becomes fragmented, drawings are not updated on time, and handover files require extra repair work later. In regulated and capital intensive environments, these are not minor operational inconveniences, but factors that affect quality, traceability, safety, and compliance. The growing pressure on execution and digital work processes only increases the importance of that foundation.

That is precisely what makes remote capacity substantively defensible in technical environments.

CBS reported that labor costs per hour worked in the Netherlands rose from €42.5 to €45.0 in 2024, an increase of 6 percent. That increases pressure on organizations that need to add structural capacity.

blocks.text: Conclusion

The shortage of technical talent in the Netherlands is increasingly evolving from a recruitment problem into a capacity challenge. The combination of ageing, limited inflow, high replacement demand, rising labor costs, and growing digital complexity means that engineering and industrial companies need to rethink their team model. Recent insights from UWV, Wij Techniek, CBS, and other sources do not point to a rapid normalization of the labor market.

en.title: 8 redenen waarom talent op afstand een antwoord is op capaciteitsdruk in techniek en industrie
en.description: The shortage of technical staff calls for structural choices. Read 8 reasons why remote talent is an answer to capacity pressure in engineering and industry.

blocks.text: Whitepaper

The shortage of technical talent in the Netherlands is increasingly shifting from a temporary recruitment issue to a structural capacity challenge. UWV reports that in the first half of 2025, there were an average of 400,000 vacancies per quarter. It classifies the labor market in all regions as tight or very tight, with engineering, ICT, and construction among the sectors where pressure remains particularly high.

Sector specific forecasts confirm that this pressure is unlikely to ease soon. Wij Techniek expects that the installation engineering sector will need a total of 121,000 new people between 2025 and 2029. Much of that demand is replacement demand, driven by the expected outflow of around 118,000 employees in the same period. Techniek Nederland uses the same forecast to underline that the sector is facing a long term workforce challenge.

blocks.text: From labor shortage to capacity challenge

Many organizations still approach tight labor markets primarily as a recruitment issue. That is understandable, but incomplete. A vacancy that remains open for months is usually only the visible symptom. Beneath it lie increasing workload, backlogs in documentation, delays in preparation, fragmented data, and growing dependence on a small group of scarce senior specialists.

blocks.text: That distinction matters. A recruitment problem calls for more inflow. A capacity problem calls for a different way of organizing work. In engineering and industry, that second question has become more urgent because sustainability programs, digitalization, and infrastructure projects are increasing demand for technical capacity, while the labor market remains tight. In its Digital Decade Country Report, the European Commission also points to persistent shortages of ICT specialists and pressure on higher education in the Netherlands.

blocks.text: From that perspective, remote talent is most relevant as a structural addition to the existing team model. Not as a replacement for all local roles, but as a way to organize scarce capacity differently and more robustly.

blocks.text: 1. Remote talent expands the talent pool in a persistently tight market

The first reason is the most fundamental. As long as organizations search mainly locally or nationally, they compete with other employers in the same limited and overheated talent pool. In a market where UWV signals persistent labor shortages and the engineering sector must absorb both growth and replacement demand in the coming years, that makes organizations vulnerable.

blocks.text: For a growing number of roles in engineering and industry, physical proximity is not always the deciding factor. Expanding the talent pool is therefore not an abstract advantage, but a direct response to a labor market that locally does not offer enough capacity.

blocks.text: 2. Remote talent makes organizations less dependent on local outflow and education dynamics

The second reason is more strategic. Organizations that rely almost entirely on one national labor market for structural capacity are also fully exposed to the outflow, ageing, and educational choices within that same market. The Wij Techniek forecast shows how heavily replacement demand will weigh in the coming years. At the same time, UWV underlines that labor market tightness remains persistent across virtually all regions.

In that sense, remote capacity is not only an answer to today’s shortages, but also a way to make the workforce less vulnerable to tomorrow’s labor market pressures.

blocks.text: 3. Remote talent makes capacity scalable and continuous

A third reason is that remote talent fits a structural shortage better than a model that depends primarily on urgent temporary hiring, overtime, or internal task redistribution. Temporary solutions may ease pressure, but they rarely build lasting capacity. A structural model works differently: professionals who operate within the same processes, systems, and meeting structures over a longer period build knowledge of files, work rhythms, and standards. As a result, their effectiveness increases over time.

When engineers, project managers, and technical coordinators spend a large share of their time on revisions, documentation, reporting, checks, and preparatory work, pressure increases precisely on the people needed for design decisions, technical judgment, and risk management. Signals from the sector about the shortage of engineers make it clear how valuable that time has become.

blocks.text: Remote talent can help break that pattern by structurally supporting execution focused and process oriented activities. That allows senior time to shift back toward the work where it adds the greatest value. In a market where experienced technical professionals remain scarce, this is not a marginal optimization issue, but a core component of capacity policy.

blocks.text: 5. Remote talent strengthens the foundation under quality, documentation, and compliance

In engineering and industry, a capacity problem often becomes most visible in the work that gets postponed. As built documentation falls behind, data becomes fragmented, drawings are not updated on time, and handover files require extra repair work later. In regulated and capital intensive environments, these are not minor operational inconveniences, but factors that affect quality, traceability, safety, and compliance. The growing pressure on execution and digital work processes only increases the importance of that foundation.

blocks.text: Additional remote capacity is therefore especially relevant when it supports processes that underpin operational reliability, such as document control, data management, reporting, revisions, and project support. The benefit then lies not only in saving time, but also in reducing rework and creating a more controllable operation. That is precisely what makes remote capacity substantively defensible in technical environments.

blocks.text: 6. Remote talent provides access to up to date knowledge and new skill sets

In addition to extra capacity, international remote talent can also provide access to more recently trained professionals and newer specializations. That matters in a market where the Netherlands is facing shortages of ICT specialists and pressure on higher education. The European Commission explicitly notes that these shortages continue to weigh on the Dutch digital labor market.

blocks.text: At the same time, international sources show that markets such as India are educating large numbers of professionals in technical and digital fields. That does not mean every international talent pool is automatically better in quality, but it does support the point that remote models can provide access to current knowledge and skill sets that are scarce locally.

blocks.text: 7. Remote talent can offer a stronger price quality ratio

The seventh reason is economic. In a market characterized by rising scarcity, organizations naturally take a closer look at the relationship between cost, quality, and continuity. CBS reported that labor costs per hour worked in the Netherlands rose from €42.5 to €45.0 in 2024, an increase of 6 percent. That increases pressure on organizations that need to add structural capacity.

blocks.text: International remote models can then become attractive, not because lower cost is the goal in itself, but because they create room to add structural capacity at a different cost profile than is often achievable locally. ILOSTAT shows average monthly employee earnings in India of INR 20,812 for 2024. These figures are not methodologically comparable one to one with Dutch hourly labor costs, but they do illustrate that cost structures differ significantly across countries. That creates room for a model in which availability, quality, and cost can be balanced differently.

blocks.text: 8. Remote talent can increase the diversity of technical teams

The eighth reason is strategic and cultural. In the Netherlands, the inflow of women into technical education remains limited. In 2024, CBS reported that 28 percent of boys in secondary education chose technical subjects, compared with 10 percent of girls. EIGE also shows that women make up 19 percent of ICT specialists in the Netherlands. This makes clear that many organizations are searching locally within a relatively narrow talent base.

blocks.text: International talent pools can create additional opportunities on this point. That gap shows that barriers still exist there as well, but it also underlines that the education pipeline is broader. For companies that struggle to find female technical professionals locally, international sourcing can therefore also contribute to more diversity in teams.

blocks.text: Conclusion

The shortage of technical talent in the Netherlands is increasingly evolving from a recruitment problem into a capacity challenge. The combination of ageing, limited inflow, high replacement demand, rising labor costs, and growing digital complexity means that engineering and industrial companies need to rethink their team model. Recent insights from UWV, Wij Techniek, CBS, and other sources do not point to a rapid normalization of the labor market.

nl.title: 8 redenen waarom talent op afstand een antwoord is op capaciteitsdruk in techniek en industrie
nl.description: Het tekort aan technisch personeel vraagt om structurele keuzes. Lees 8 redenen waarom talent op afstand een antwoord is op capaciteitsdruk in techniek en industrie.

blocks.text: Het tekort aan technisch personeel in Nederland is steeds minder een tijdelijk recruitmentvraagstuk en steeds meer een structureel capaciteitsprobleem. UWV meldt dat er in de eerste helft van 2025 gemiddeld 400.000 vacatures per kwartaal openstonden. Daarbij kwalificeert UWV de arbeidsmarkt in alle arbeidsmarktregio’s als krap of zeer krap, met onder meer techniek, ICT en bouw als sectoren waar de spanning groot blijft.

blocks.text: Van personeelstekort naar capaciteitsvraagstuk

Ook sectorspecifieke prognoses laten zien dat deze druk niet snel verdwijnt. Wij Techniek verwacht dat in de installatietechniek in de periode 2025 tot en met 2029 in totaal 121.000 nieuwe mensen nodig zijn. Daarachter zit vooral een grote vervangingsvraag, met een verwachte uitstroom van circa 118.000 medewerkers in dezelfde periode. Techniek Nederland gebruikt dezelfde prognose om te onderstrepen dat de sector voor een langdurige personele opgave staat.

De prognose van Wij Techniek laat zien hoe zwaar die vervangingsvraag de komende jaren weegt. UWV onderstreept tegelijk dat krapte in vrijwel alle regio’s aanhoudt.

blocks.text: 3. Talent op afstand maakt capaciteit schaalbaar en continu

Een derde reden is dat talent op afstand beter past bij een structureel tekort dan een model dat vooral leunt op spoedinhuur, overwerk of interne herverdeling van taken. Tijdelijke oplossingen verlichten soms de druk, maar bouwen zelden duurzame capaciteit op. Een structureel model werkt anders: professionals die langere tijd in dezelfde processen, systemen en overlegstructuren meedraaien, bouwen kennis op van dossiers, werkritme en standaarden. Daardoor neemt hun effectiviteit in de tijd toe.

In gereguleerde en kapitaalintensieve omgevingen zijn dit geen kleine operationele ongemakken, maar factoren die kwaliteit, traceerbaarheid, veiligheid en compliance raken.

blocks.text: 6. Talent op afstand geeft toegang tot actuele kennis en nieuwe skillsets

Naast extra capaciteit kan internationale remote inzet ook toegang geven tot recenter opgeleide professionals en nieuwe specialisaties. Dat is relevant in een markt waar Nederland te maken heeft met tekorten aan specialistische digitale en technische profielen, terwijl werkprocessen steeds sterker digitaliseren. UWV benadrukt bovendien dat technologische ontwikkelingen en AI leiden tot verschuivingen in taken en vaardigheden, waardoor bijscholing en nieuwe skillsets steeds belangrijker worden.

Voor organisaties in techniek en industrie kan het gaan om toegang tot kennis die lokaal schaars is, of om een snellere aanvulling op bestaande teams met profielen die recent zijn opgeleid in actuele domeinen. Het argument is dus niet dat internationale talentpools per definitie beter zijn, maar dat zij aanvullende kennis en specialistische vaardigheden kunnen ontsluiten die lokaal niet altijd direct beschikbaar zijn.

blocks.text: 7. Talent op afstand kan een sterkere prijs-kwaliteitverhouding bieden

De zevende reden is economisch. In een markt met oplopende schaarste kijken organisaties vanzelf scherper naar de verhouding tussen prijs, kwaliteit en continuïteit. CBS meldde dat de loonkosten per gewerkt uur in Nederland in 2024 stegen van €42,5 naar €45,0, een toename van 6 procent. Dat verhoogt de druk op organisaties die structureel extra capaciteit nodig hebben.

blocks.text: Internationale remote modellen kunnen dan aantrekkelijk zijn, niet omdat lagere kosten op zichzelf het doel zijn, maar omdat ze ruimte bieden om structurele capaciteit toe te voegen tegen een ander kostenprofiel dan lokaal vaak haalbaar is. Dat vraagt wel om een zorgvuldige afweging. De kern is niet zo goedkoop mogelijk inkopen, maar een werkbaar evenwicht vinden tussen beschikbaarheid, kwaliteit en kosten in een krappe markt. Juist daardoor is prijs geen los argument, maar onderdeel van een bredere afweging over capaciteit.

blocks.text: 8. Talent op afstand kan de diversiteit van technische teams vergroten

De achtste reden is strategisch en cultureel. In Nederland blijft de instroom van vrouwen in techniek beperkt. CBS meldde in 2024 dat 28 procent van de jongens in het voortgezet onderwijs voor technische vakken koos, tegenover 10 procent van de meisjes. Op Europees niveau ligt het aandeel vrouwen onder ICT specialisten rond één op de vijf. Dat maakt duidelijk dat veel organisaties lokaal in een relatief smalle talentbasis zoeken.

blocks.text: Conclusie

Het tekort aan technisch personeel in Nederland ontwikkelt zich steeds duidelijker van een recruitmentprobleem naar een capaciteitsvraagstuk. en.title: A follow-up on the ISO 42001 programme at WorldEmp, from setting it up to demonstrable progress
en.description: Read how WorldEmp is taking further steps in ISO 42001, with an internal audit, AI awareness and a firmer grip on the full lifecycle of AI applications.

blocks.text: By: Peter van Londen, COO WorldEmp

Three weeks ago we shared how WorldEmp applies ISO 42001 in practice. In that article we showed how we are building a solid AI Management System, with attention to engineering, quality assurance, training, guardrails and data governance.
Sindsdien hebben we in datzelfde traject opnieuw concrete stappen gezet.
blocks.html: Sindsdien hebben we in datzelfde traject opnieuw concrete stappen gezet.

blocks.alt: offshore oil, gas, wind, jack-up, energy transition

blocks.text: ISO 42001 in practice: from engineering to data governance
A Sustainable Alternative: Digital Knowledge Migrants
Governance and architecture
In the area of governance and architecture, we have achieved the following results:
blocks.html: In the area of governance and architecture, we have achieved the following results:

items: We have developed a comprehensive AI Implementation High-Level Architecture & Design Playbook. This links ISO 42001 requirements to practical controls, a cloud-native architecture based on technologies such as Azure, AKS, Next.js and FastAPI, and a gated AI lifecycle delivery model.
We have set up clear governance structures, including RACI matrices and reference architectures for scalable, secure and ethical AI SaaS delivery.

blocks.text: Responsible AI Impact Assessment

items: For our generative AI SaaS environment, we have carried out a comprehensive Responsible AI Impact Assessment:
This assessment covers, among other things, stakeholder mapping, fairness, privacy, human oversight and risk mitigations.
The approach is fully aligned with the Microsoft Responsible AI Standard and ISO 42001.

blocks.text: Risk and incident management

items: Risk and incidents are structurally embedded in our AIMS:

We have created AI Impact Assessment Registers and Risk Assessment & Treatment Templates to systematically identify, evaluate and mitigate risks. This includes risks related to bias, privacy, security, reliability, operations and regulation.
We have implemented an Information Security Incident & Investigation Framework with AI-specific enhancements, automated reporting and root cause analysis workflows.

blocks.text: Our approach and principles

items: Three principles are central to our approach:
Human-in-the-loop oversight for high-impact decisions.
Continuous monitoring, incident response and improvement cycles.
Transparent stakeholder communication and clear disclosure of AI interactions.

nl.description: Lees hoe WorldEmp verdere stappen zet in ISO 42001, met een interne audit, AI awareness en meer grip op de volledige lifecycle van AI toepassingen.

blocks.text: Door: Peter van Londen, COO WorldEmp

Drie weken geleden deelden we hoe WorldEmp ISO 42001 in de praktijk toepast. In dat artikel lieten we zien hoe we werken aan een stevig AI Management System, met aandacht voor engineering, quality assurance, training, guardrails en datagovernance.
blocks.html: Drie weken geleden deelden we hoe WorldEmp ISO 42001 in de praktijk toepast. In dat artikel lieten we zien hoe we werken aan een stevig AI Management System, met aandacht voor engineering, quality assurance, training, guardrails en datagovernance.

blocks.text: De volgende stap in ons ISO 42001 traject
Interne audit als volgende stap

Zo hebben we onze eerste interne audit succesvol afgerond. Daarbij hebben we niet alleen gekeken naar de opzet van ons managementsysteem, maar ook naar de onderliggende documentatie en bewijslast van lopende AI toepassingen. Dat geeft ons een duidelijker beeld van waar we staan en bevestigt dat de basis goed is ingericht.
blocks.html: Zo hebben we onze eerste interne audit succesvol afgerond. Daarbij hebben we niet alleen gekeken naar de opzet van ons managementsysteem, maar ook naar de onderliggende documentatie en bewijslast van lopende AI toepassingen. Dat geeft ons een duidelijker beeld van waar we staan en bevestigt dat de basis goed is ingericht.

blocks.text: Bewustwording in de organisatie

Ook op organisatieniveau hebben we verdere voortgang geboekt. Medewerkers zijn inmiddels meegenomen in het verantwoord gebruik van AI binnen de kaders van ISO 42001. Daarmee bouwen we niet alleen aan processen en documentatie, maar ook aan bewustwording en een gedeelde manier van werken.
blocks.html: Ook op organisatieniveau hebben we verdere voortgang geboekt. Medewerkers zijn inmiddels meegenomen in het verantwoord gebruik van AI binnen de kaders van ISO 42001. Daarmee bouwen we niet alleen aan processen en documentatie, maar ook aan bewustwording en een gedeelde manier van werken.

blocks.text: Grip op de volledige lifecycle

Daarnaast hebben we onze workflows verder uitgewerkt en een lifecycle applicatie ingericht voor onze AI oplossingen. Hierdoor kunnen we per toepassing gestructureerd kijken naar risico’s, beheersmaatregelen en verantwoordelijkheden, vanaf het eerste concept tot en met implementatie en beheer.
blocks.html: Daarnaast hebben we onze workflows verder uitgewerkt en een lifecycle applicatie ingericht voor onze AI oplossingen. Hierdoor kunnen we per toepassing gestructureerd kijken naar risico’s, beheersmaatregelen en verantwoordelijkheden, vanaf het eerste concept tot en met implementatie en beheer.

blocks.text: Van inrichting naar toepassing

Deze stap is een logisch vervolg op ons eerdere bericht. Waar de vorige update vooral liet zien hoe we ISO 42001 inhoudelijk hebben ingebed in onze manier van werken, laat deze update zien dat die inrichting ook daadwerkelijk wordt getoetst en toegepast in de praktijk.

en.title: KUBO ziet kracht van samenwerking in India
en.description: KUBO visited the team in India and saw at first hand what structural international collaboration produces: trust, ownership and colleagues who are genuinely part of the team.

blocks.text: India feels close when working together really makes you part of the team

Sometimes a visit says more than months of online meetings. That is what happened during KUBO's recent visit to their colleagues in India. What began with two professionals through WorldEmp has grown into a team of eleven who contribute to KUBO's projects every day.

For Wouter Kuiper, CEO of KUBO, the week made one thing visible above all. Distance says little when people are genuinely part of the same team. No external help desk, no separate shell, but colleagues who take responsibility and make a visible impact.

For WorldEmp, this is a familiar signal. Large technology companies have been deliberately building their innovation capacity in India for quite some time. Not just to scale, but to gain access to specialized expertise in engineering, product development, and AI.
blocks.html: For WorldEmp, this is a familiar signal. Large technology companies have been deliberately building their innovation capacity in India for quite some time. Not just to scale, but to gain access to specialized expertise in engineering, product development, and AI.

blocks.text: This aligns with what we see in the market every day: many Dutch companies want to grow, but run into the same local constraints. Skilled technical professionals are scarce, vacancies remain open for long periods, and projects often require more capacity than is available internally.
blocks.html: This aligns with what we see in the market every day: many Dutch companies want to grow, but run into the same local constraints. Skilled technical professionals are scarce, vacancies remain open for long periods, and projects often require more capacity than is available internally.

blocks.text: The shortage requires a different approach

That is why we look at the shortage of highly educated technical talent differently. Not as a temporary recruitment issue, but as a structural capacity challenge. For many organizations, the solution is not just searching longer in a tight local market, but intelligently adding international professionals who can integrate directly into your team. Not as an external layer, but as remote colleagues who contribute to continuity, speed, and quality.

India is playing an increasingly important role in this. For companies looking to accelerate in software development, data, or AI, it is a serious source of reinforcement. This is where a significant opportunity lies for Dutch companies: access to professionals who can quickly integrate and immediately add value to the existing team.

en.title: Why Digital Knowledge Migrants Are Better Than Traditional Knowledge Migrants
en.description: Digital knowledge migrants offer a modern and efficient solution to the growing shortage of highly skilled specialists in the Netherlands. Unlike traditional knowledge migrants, who physically relocate to the country, digital knowledge migrants can work remotely, allowing companies to attract talent more quickly and flexibly. This reduces costs, expands the talent pool, and minimizes administrative and logistical barriers. This page explores why digital knowledge migrants are a better choice for companies seeking innovative and scalable workforce solutions.

A knowledge migrant is a highly skilled foreign professional who comes to the Netherlands to work in industries facing talent shortages. blocks.text: Why choose a remote team?

Choosing a remote team offers a wide range of benefits. First, it gives you access to a global talent pool. By not limiting yourself to local candidates, you can attract the best professionals from around the world. This not only increases diversity within your team, but also brings in new perspectives and innovations.

blocks.text: Second, there are clear cost advantages. blocks.text: Main challenges of remote working

Despite the many benefits, remote working also brings its own challenges. One of the biggest challenges is communication. In a traditional office environment, team members can easily discuss matters face-to-face. This is not possible with remote working, which can lead to misunderstandings and inefficiencies.

blocks.text: Tips for successful remote cooperation
To overcome these challenges and be successful with a remote team, there are several best practices you can follow.
blocks.html: To overcome these challenges and be successful with a remote team, there are several best practices you can follow.

items: First, it is important to establish clear communication channels. This includes not only choosing the right tools, such as video meetings and chat apps, but also establishing communication guidelines. For example, who should be kept informed of what information, and in what way?

It is also essential to hold regular check-ins and team meetings. This not only helps keep everyone up to date on progress and any problems, but again strengthens team cohesion. Setting clear goals and expectations is also very important. When everyone knows exactly what is expected of them and the deadlines, this can help increase productivity and reduce misunderstandings.

Flexibility and trust are also important. Trust your team members to deliver their work on time and with the right quality, and be flexible with working hours. This can help foster a positive work culture and increase motivation.

blocks.text: Our thought on working successfully with remote colleagues is mainly to use your common sense and treat your co-workers as if they were sitting next to you in the office. Good onboarding, including them in all meetings, as well as having conversations as if you were at the coffee machine. Ask about the weekend and how things are going at home. It's as simple as that!
