blocks.text: Waarom kiezen voor een remote team?

Het kiezen voor een remote team biedt een scala aan voordelen. Ten eerste is er de toegang tot een wereldwijde talentenpool. Door niet beperkt te zijn tot lokale kandidaten, kunnen bedrijven de beste mensen van over de hele wereld aantrekken. Dit vergroot niet alleen de diversiteit binnen het team, maar ook de verschillende perspectieven en innovaties die zij met zich meebrengen.
blocks.html: Het kiezen voor een remote team biedt een scala aan voordelen. Ten eerste is er de toegang tot een wereldwijde talentenpool. Door niet beperkt te zijn tot lokale kandidaten, kunnen bedrijven de beste mensen van over de hele wereld aantrekken. Dit vergroot niet alleen de diversiteit binnen het team, maar ook de verschillende perspectieven en innovaties die zij met zich meebrengen.

blocks.text: Ten tweede zijn er kostenvoordelen. Het inhuren van remote medewerkers kan aanzienlijk goedkoper zijn dan het aannemen van lokaal personeel, vooral wanneer je rekening houdt met de kosten voor kantoorruimte, apparatuur en andere gerelateerde uitgaven. Bovendien kunnen bedrijven dankzij remote werken flexibelere werkregelingen aanbieden, wat kan leiden tot een hogere werknemerstevredenheid en retentie.

Het inhuren van remote medewerkers kan aanzienlijk goedkoper zijn dan het aannemen van lokaal personeel, vooral wanneer je rekening houdt met de kosten voor kantoorruimte, apparatuur en andere gerelateerde uitgaven. Bovendien kunnen bedrijven dankzij remote werken flexibelere werkregelingen aanbieden, wat kan leiden tot een hogere werknemerstevredenheid en retentie.

blocks.text: Ten derde kan de productiviteit toenemen. Onderzoek heeft aangetoond dat remote medewerkers vaak productiever zijn dan hun kantoorwerkende tegenhangers. Zonder de afleiding van een druk kantoor kunnen zij zich beter concentreren op hun werk.

blocks.text: Belangrijkste uitdagingen van remote werken

Ondanks de vele voordelen, brengt remote werken ook zijn eigen uitdagingen met zich mee. Een van de grootste uitdagingen is communicatie. In een traditionele kantooromgeving kunnen teamleden gemakkelijk face-to-face overleggen. Bij remote werken is dit niet mogelijk, wat kan leiden tot misverstanden en inefficiënties.

blocks.text: Een andere uitdaging is het opbouwen en onderhouden van teamcohesie. Het is moeilijker om een sterke teamcultuur te ontwikkelen wanneer teamleden elkaar niet dagelijks persoonlijk zien. Dit kan leiden tot gevoelens van isolatie en vervreemding, wat de samenwerking en motivatie kan verminderen.

blocks.text: Ook de technologie kan een struikelblok zijn. Niet alle teamleden hebben toegang tot dezelfde technologieën of weten hoe ze deze effectief moeten gebruiken. Dit kan leiden tot technische problemen en vertragingen in projecten.

blocks.text: Tips voor succesvolle samenwerking op afstand
Om deze uitdagingen te overwinnen en succesvol te zijn met een remote team, zijn er verschillende best practices die je kunt volgen.
blocks.html: Om deze uitdagingen te overwinnen en succesvol te zijn met een remote team, zijn er verschillende best practices die je kunt volgen.

items: Ten eerste is het belangrijk om duidelijke communicatiekanalen op te zetten. Dit omvat niet alleen het kiezen van de juiste tools, zoals videovergaderingen en chat-apps, maar ook het vaststellen van communicatierichtlijnen. Wie moet bijvoorbeeld op de hoogte worden gehouden van welke informatie, en op welke manier?

Daarnaast is het essentieel om regelmatige check-ins en teamvergaderingen te houden. Dit helpt niet alleen om iedereen op de hoogte te houden van de voortgang en eventuele problemen, maar versterkt ook weer de teamcohesie. Het instellen van duidelijke doelen en verwachtingen is ook erg belangrijk. Wanneer iedereen precies weet wat er van hen wordt verwacht en welke deadlines er zijn, kan dit helpen om de productiviteit te verhogen en misverstanden te verminderen.

Flexibiliteit en vertrouwen zijn eveneens belangrijk. Vertrouw je teamleden om hun werk op tijd en met de juiste kwaliteit af te leveren, en wees flexibel met werkuren. Dit kan helpen om een positieve werkcultuur te bevorderen en de motivatie te verhogen.

blocks.text: Onze gedachte over succesvol samenwerken met remote collega’s is vooral om je gezond verstand te gebruiken en met je medewerkers om te gaan alsof ze naast je op kantoor zitten. Door hen als ieder ander te behandelen, merk je heel snel dat het totaal niet lastig is om met remote collega’s te werken. Wat valt daar onder andere onder? Een goede onboarding, hen betrekken bij alle overleggen, maar ook gesprekken voeren alsof je bij het koffieapparaat staat. Vraag naar het weekend en hoe het thuis gaat. Zo simpel is het!

blocks.text: As of 1 July, WorldEmp will officially establish itself at RDM Rotterdam. Following a welcoming start-up period at iTanks, WorldEmp now has a permanent place in an environment where innovation, technology and entrepreneurship come together.

Het bedrijf uit de IJmond-regio, met vestigingen in Velsen-Zuid, Rotterdam, Eindhoven en India, opent daarmee een eigen kantoor in de Medische Dienst. Na een gastvrije opstartperiode bij iTanks krijgt WorldEmp een vaste plek in een omgeving waar innovatie, techniek en ondernemerschap samenkomen.

en.title: WorldEmp recruits digital knowledge migrants for Brainport
en.description: WorldEmp, which is setting up in Eindhoven, recruits highly educated staff in India to work for Dutch companies.

blocks.text: Breakfast in India, but working ‘in Eindhoven’: WorldEmp recruits ‘digital knowledge migrants’ for Brainport

Eindhoven - Brainport has to work more intelligently to solve its large shortage of knowledge workers. The Dutch company WorldEmp, which is setting up in Eindhoven, recruits highly educated staff in India who go to work there for Dutch companies. As digital knowledge migrants.

Why would you, as a company, try to bring thousands of foreign knowledge workers to your country if they could just as well do the same work digitally in their own? That was entrepreneur Frank Korf's foresight seven years ago, when he was doing business with Indian companies.

Korf: “Indians are often highly educated and sharp; they are active and enterprising. I saw companies bringing people over from India to the Netherlands, and that was not always a success. The pressure on society here is considerable. Where do you house thousands of knowledge migrants? They have no network to fall back on. And in time they miss their families and go back. Would it not be nicer if they could work in their own country and culture, close to their families, to our standards? That is how it started.”
Covid brought a turning point

In 2014 WorldEmp opened an office in the Indian city of Pune, from which staff work for a range of Dutch companies. A second site in Bangalore soon followed. The offices meet the highest ISO standards, according to Korf, the fit-out matches the parent company and terms of employment are the same as in the Netherlands. Companies were wary of remote working at first, but the coronavirus pandemic brought a shift in thinking. Korf: “Now there is a real conviction that working remotely works. We provide engineers for Vogels of Helmond, who design scaffolding, but also for Van Lent Systems of Oss, and we work for manufacturing, such as Tata Steel. Now we are going to focus on Eindhoven and the surrounding area.”
A shortage of staff

WorldEmp claims to be able to meet demand for specific staff within six weeks at most. Korf: “In Brainport there is a need for software developers and specialists in industrial automation. A company comes to us with a set of competencies; our psychologists in the Netherlands draw up a profile from them, and our recruiters in India go out and recruit. Candidates have to have at least 6 years of experience and a university or higher professional education. Within a couple of weeks we have a good thirty candidates. We test for language skills, talent and speed of development. Experience shows that six percent of candidates are left. The client then speaks to them digitally, because the personal click and the match have to be there too.”
Breakfast in India, work in Eindhoven, dinner at the table with your family”
Frank Korf, Founder and CEO at WorldEmp

“We want people to stay a long time, to be loyal. There are companies who have been working with our people for four to five years now. You really do gain a colleague, only digitally through a screen. Our philosophy is that our people have breakfast in India, work in Eindhoven and have dinner at home at the table with their family.”
A piece of the puzzle

TU/e professor Maarten Steinbuch is enthusiastic. He sees part of a solution to the shortage of knowledge workers in the Brainport region. Steinbuch got to know WorldEmp in 2019 during a trade mission to India with the Royal Family. He now sits on the Advisory Board. Steinbuch: “For years I have worked to secure enough staff for this region. Brainport is growing enormously. ASML alone has 6,000 vacancies. But there are bottlenecks here in liveability. We cannot build enough homes; there are not enough facilities. On top of that, a good share of the Indian people working here want to go back after five years. Understandable if your family lives there, but it means the companies that invested in them lose them. These people can be retained through WorldEmp. Brainport has to keep growing. This solves a piece of the puzzle.”

blocks.text: the indispensable force in oil, gas and offshore wind

In the world of offshore energy, engineers are simply indispensable. Whether it is oil and gas platforms or large-scale offshore wind farms, nothing gets off the ground without specialist engineers. Or rather, nothing gets into the water. They are the quiet force behind progress at sea. Offshore structural engineers design platforms and installations. Marine mechanical engineers keep every mechanical system running, and data engineers use artificial intelligence to make processes smarter, safer and more efficient. Their knowledge and precision form the backbone of an industry in which innovation and safety go hand in hand.

blocks.alt: Zonder engineers geen offshore-industrie: de onmisbare kracht in olie, gas en wind op zee
Zonder engineers geen offshore-industrie

blocks.text: The Dutch maritime and offshore industry is in a strong growth phase. According to the NMT-IRO sector annual report 2024, newbuild production rose by 27 percent last year, while total ship tonnage rose by as much as 59 percent. That growth brings not only more work but, above all, more complexity. Every new project demands a higher level of design, integration and data-driven engineering. That puts further pressure on available capacity. The sector itself has been warning for some time of a structural shortage of technical talent. Both trade bodies and policymakers stress that more hands - and more thinking power - are needed to sustain the growth. Intake from technical education, however, is lagging behind, which leaves companies struggling to find enough engineers.

This combination of growth, complexity and scarcity makes it clear that the availability of engineers sets the pace of innovation. Without their expertise, progress stalls. Projects are delayed, knowledge disappears and competitive position comes under pressure. Engineers are the engine behind the energy transition at sea. They translate ideas and data into working solutions that make the sector fit for the future.
A Sustainable Alternative: Digital Knowledge Migrants

At WorldEmp, we believe there’s a smarter way. Our model focuses on digital knowledge migrants: highly educated international professionals who work for Dutch companies directly from their home countries, fully integrated into the team.

blocks.text: De Nederlandse maritieme en offshore-industrie maakt momenteel een sterke groeifase door. Die groei brengt niet alleen meer werk met zich mee, maar vooral meer complexiteit. Elk nieuw project vraagt om een hoger niveau van ontwerp, integratie en datagedreven engineering. Daarmee neemt de druk op de beschikbare capaciteit verder toe. De sector zelf waarschuwt al enige tijd voor een structureel tekort aan technisch talent. Zowel brancheorganisaties als beleidsmakers benadrukken dat er meer handen én denkkracht nodig zijn om de groei vol te houden. De instroom vanuit technische opleidingen blijft echter achter, waardoor bedrijven moeite hebben om voldoende engineers te vinden.

blocks.text: The bridge between the Netherlands and India
Culture

In today's globalized labor market, culture plays a crucial role in the success of international collaborations. Understanding and appreciating cultural differences is not only important for personal relationships but also for professional success. At WorldEmp, we recognize the significance of cultural alignment, especially in the collaboration between the Netherlands and India. These two countries have unique cultures that, when navigated correctly, can lead to a rich and fruitful partnership.

blocks.text: Cultural differences between the Netherlands and India

Dutch work culture is known for its directness, equality, and pragmatic approach. Dutch people value openness, clear communication, and have an informal manner in the workplace. On the other hand, India has a more hierarchical work culture, where respect for elders and authority are deeply rooted. Communication can be more indirect, and there is often a strong emphasis on group harmony.

blocks.text: Local vs. Global
Bridging the talent gap with WorldEmp

In a world where the demand for highly skilled personnel is growing faster than the supply, Dutch and European companies face a significant challenge. Locally, there is a considerable shortage of specialized talent, which can hinder innovation and growth. However, if we broaden our perspective to a global scale, an ocean of untapped talent reveals itself. This is where WorldEmp plays a crucial role, acting as a bridge between local business needs and global talent pools.

blocks.text: The local talent shortage

Netherlands and Europe are grappling with a growing shortage of highly skilled personnel in crucial sectors such as technology, engineering, and healthcare. This gap between demand and supply drives up competition for local talent, increases salary costs, and slows down essential projects. This shortage not only limits companies' capacity to innovate and expand but also acts as a brake on economic growth in the region.

en.title: How we Recruit and Select Talent
en.description: At WorldEmp we carefully select based on technical skills, soft skills, cultural fit and business suitability.

blocks.text: Recruitment and selection process

At WorldEmp, we employ an extensive selection process based on four pillars. We do not simply pull candidates from a large database; instead, we evaluate technical skills and 'soft skills'. Additionally, we ensure that candidates are a good fit with Dutch culture and your company.
blocks.html: At WorldEmp, we employ an extensive selection process based on four pillars. We do not simply pull candidates from a large database; instead, we evaluate technical skills and 'soft skills'. Additionally, we ensure that candidates are a good fit with Dutch culture and your company.

blocks.text: Extensive selection procedure

Over the past 20 years, we have built a large global network, enabling us to quickly find the right people. Within just two to six weeks, we can add a colleague, or an entire team, with the desired expertise to your organization. We match the right people to your company, ensuring minimal staff turnover.
blocks.html: Over the past 20 years, we have built a large global network, enabling us to quickly find the right people. Within just two to six weeks, we can add a colleague, or an entire team, with the desired expertise to your organization. We match the right people to your company, ensuring minimal staff turnover.

blocks.text: After an initial selection, we follow a procedure according to these steps:

blocks.alt: Recruiter WorldEmp

blocks.text: Vaardigheden

First of all we look, naturally, at the expertise you have asked for. Every candidate at WorldEmp holds a bachelor's or master's degree and has at least six years of work experience. On top of that we run several assessments.

At short notice we can supply colleagues with expertise in: data analysis, engineering, finance and software development such as JavaScript, SAP, SQL, C++, Oracle, .Net, PHP, Java, design, testing, AutoCAD, Pro-E, SolidWorks, graphic design and more.
Language proficiency

Effective collaboration hinges on communication, so we ensure that colleagues are always virtually present and that they possess excellent English skills. This is tested by native speakers who thoroughly interview during the selection process.

blocks.text: Even after employees have started, their English language skills continue to be developed. For this, we collaborate with a language institute, focusing on oral skills, such as pronunciation and accent.

In addition to assessments focused on technical skills and extensive interviews, we also administer a psychological test under the supervision of an experienced assessment specialist. The results determine whether a candidate can be hired.

blocks.text: Culture test
Of course, a colleague must also fit into your company. Therefore, we also carefully consider potential cultural differences.

blocks.text: Remote Working with the WorldEmp Concept

As remote working increasingly becomes the new standard for companies worldwide, the WorldEmp concept offers a unique approach that elevates the benefits of remote work to a higher level. By leveraging digital knowledge migrants, we ensure that your company gains direct access to a global talent pool, without the traditional hindrances of international relocation and associated logistical challenges. Here's how the WorldEmp concept can enhance the implementation and benefits of remote working in your company.

blocks.text: The benefits of remote working and digital knowledge migrants

items: ​Access to global talent: Digital knowledge migrants enable your company to tap into highly qualified professionals from around the world, expanding beyond the constraints of the local labor market. You're fishing in a much larger pond than just in the Netherlands; in fact, you're casting your net into an ocean of professionals!
Flexibility: By utilizing digital knowledge migrants, you can adapt flexibly to changing needs and projects without worrying about location restrictions.

Cost savings: Hiring digital knowledge migrants is cost-effective for your company, as you incur no additional expenses for office space, visa fees, or relocation allowances. Everything is arranged without extra paperwork or hidden costs.

Faster recruitment: Digital knowledge migrants can often be hired more quickly than local employees, allowing you to scale up your projects faster and meet deadlines. Say goodbye to saying "No" to projects!

Multiple skills and perspectives: Digital knowledge migrants bring a diverse set of skills, knowledge, and experiences, offering valuable perspectives and contributing to innovation within the company. They bring a fresh perspective and rejuvenate your company.

Increased productivity: Because digital knowledge migrants often work autonomously and independently, they can deliver higher productivity by being less distracted and more focused on their tasks. They aren't distracted by walk-in clients or colleagues asking for ad-hoc tasks but have real focus on the work.
Scalability: By utilizing digital knowledge migrants, your company can easily scale up or down based on your needs, without the burden of recruiting and dismissing local employees.

Discover today how WorldEmp can support your transition to a successful remote-working organization.

nl.description: WorldEmp's digitale kennismigranten bieden directe toegang tot wereldwijd talent, zonder relocatie hindernissen.

blocks.text: Terwijl remote werken steeds vaker de nieuwe standaard wordt voor bedrijven wereldwijd, biedt het WorldEmp concept een unieke benadering die de voordelen van remote werken naar een hoger niveau tilt. Door het inzetten van digitale kennismigranten, zorgen we ervoor dat jouw bedrijf direct toegang krijgt tot een globale talentenpool, zonder de traditionele hindernissen van internationale relocatie en de bijbehorende logistieke uitdagingen. Hier is hoe het WorldEmp concept de implementatie en voordelen van remote werken in jouw bedrijf kan versterken.

blocks.text: De voordelen van remote werken en digitale kennismigranten

items: Toegang tot wereldwijd talent: Digitale kennismigranten stellen jouw bedrijf in staat om toegang te krijgen tot hooggekwalificeerde professionals over de hele wereld, waardoor ze niet beperkt zijn tot de lokale arbeidsmarkt. Je vist in een veel grotere vijver dan enkel in Nederland, sterker nog; je vist in een oceaan van professionals!
Flexibiliteit: Door gebruik te maken van digitale kennismigranten kun je flexibel inspelen op veranderende behoeften en projecten zonder dat je je zorgen hoeft te maken over locatiebeperkingen.

Kostenbesparing: Het inhuren van digitale kennismigranten is kostenbesparend voor jouw bedrijf, omdat je geen extra uitgaven hebt voor kantoorruimte, visumkosten of relocatievergoedingen. Alles is geregeld zonder een extra papierwinkel of verborgen kosten.

Snellere werving: Digitale kennismigranten kunnen vaak sneller worden ingehuurd dan lokale werknemers, waardoor je jouw projecten sneller kan opschalen en deadlines kunt halen. Zeg geen "Nee" meer tegen projecten!

Diverse vaardigheden en perspectieven: Digitale kennismigranten brengen een diverse set vaardigheden, kennis en ervaringen met zich mee, waardoor ze waardevolle perspectieven kunnen bieden en bijdragen aan innovatie binnen het bedrijf. Ze hebben een andere kijk op zaken en zorgen juist voor verfrissing binnen jouw bedrijf.

Verhoogde productiviteit: Omdat digitale kennismigranten vaak autonoom en zelfstandig werken, kunnen ze een hogere productiviteit opleveren doordat ze minder worden afgeleid en meer gefocust zijn op hun taken. Ze worden niet afgeleid door klanten die binnen komen of collega's die ad-hoc dingen vragen, maar hebben echte focus op het werk.

Schaalbaarheid: Door gebruik te maken van digitale kennismigranten kun je als bedrijf gemakkelijk opschalen of inkrimpen op basis van jouw behoeften, zonder de last van het werven en ontslaan van lokale werknemers.

blocks.text: Door het WorldEmp concept te integreren in jouw remote werkstrategie, kun je de traditionele grenzen van werk overstijgen en een toekomstbestendige organisatie creëren die klaar is om de kansen van de mondiale markt te grijpen. Met toegang tot de beste talenten, ongeacht hun locatie, en de middelen om efficiënt en effectief op afstand samen te werken, zet je de volgende stap in de evolutie van jouw bedrijf. Ontdek vandaag nog hoe WorldEmp jouw transitie naar een succesvolle remote werkende organisatie kan ondersteunen.

blocks.text: The key to success in a globalizing world
Social competencies

In today's job market, technical skills are indispensable, but the power of social competencies cannot be underestimated. These skills, which revolve around how effectively you communicate, collaborate, and navigate interpersonal relationships, are essential for building successful teams, especially in an increasingly interconnected world. WorldEmp recognizes the importance of these social competencies and places them at the core of the recruitment and placement process for digital knowledge migrants.

blocks.text: The importance of social competencies

In an era where remote working and digital teams are becoming the norm, you might think that the focus would primarily be on technical skills and autonomy. However, social competencies are more important than ever. They aid in bridging cultural and geographical differences, strengthen team cohesion, and enhance overall productivity and job satisfaction.

blocks.text: The core of social competencies
What exactly are social competencies? They encompass a wide range of skills:
blocks.html: What exactly are social competencies? They encompass a wide range of skills:

items: Communication: Clearly and effectively conveying your ideas, both verbally and in writing, including listening to and understanding others.
Collaboration: Successfully working within a team, valuing diverse perspectives, and contributing to a common goal.
Adaptability: Being flexible and effectively responding to change, which is crucial in today’s rapidly evolving world.
Conflict Resolution: The ability to handle disagreements and challenges in a constructive manner.
Cultural Sensitivity: Being aware of and showing respect for cultural differences within a team.

blocks.text: WorldEmp’s approach to social competencies

At WorldEmp, we understand that the strength of a team lies not only in the sum of its technical skills but also in how team members collaborate, communicate, and solve problems. That’s why social competencies are an integral part of our selection process for digital knowledge migrants.

blocks.text: Talent management at WorldEmp

blocks.text: The world of talent management

Talent management at WorldEmp encompasses a wide range of strategies and processes that work together to bring out the best in every employee. blocks.text: How WorldEmp approaches talent management

items: Identifying Talent Needs: Everything starts with a deep understanding of your business objectives and the specific talent needs that support them. WorldEmp works closely with you to analyze not only the current but also the future requirements, helping to develop a long-term talent acquisition and development strategy.

Recruitment and Selection: Leveraging our advanced Applicant Tracking System and extensive talent network, WorldEmp ensures that only candidates who offer both the required skills and the right cultural fit are proposed and recruited. This approach guarantees a higher success rate in placements and seamless integration within teams.

Development and Training: Once talents are hired, WorldEmp is committed to their ongoing professional development. Through tailored training programs, mentorships, and continuous education, we support the growth of skills essential to your business operations. This ensures that employees not only meet the demands of their current role but also are prepared for future challenges and career opportunities.

Performance Management: Through regular assessments and feedback loops, WorldEmp helps employees optimize their performance and ensure alignment with business goals. This process includes setting clear performance indicators, regular evaluations, and constructive feedback, all designed to motivate employees and help them achieve their maximum potential.

Retention Strategies: Retaining top talent is as important as finding it. WorldEmp implements strategic retention measures ranging from competitive compensation packages to career development opportunities and a positive company culture. By focusing on employee satisfaction and engagement, WorldEmp ensures that your valuable talents remain motivated and engaged.

en.title: Your partner in the energy transition
en.description: WorldEmp accelerates your energy transition with remote engineers and data specialists - scalable capacity for wind, solar, storage and grid projects.

blocks.text: The energy transition calls for quick action, specialist expertise and dependable delivery.

As renewable generation, energy storage, grid expansion, heat solutions and smart energy systems develop further, demand for specialist professionals is growing faster than many organisations can keep up with. WorldEmp helps organisations strengthen their teams with international professionals who work remotely as integrated colleagues. This approach provides extra technical capacity without the delays and complexity of traditional recruitment, while organisations keep full control.
The capacity gap
The market moves faster than teams can grow with it

Progress in the energy transition depends on specialist expertise. Engineers, project support staff, planners, data specialists and technical coordinators are essential to delivering projects on schedule. At the same time, these professionals are getting harder to find. Long-open vacancies, the high cost of temporary support and the limits of traditional secondment models often stand in the way of the speed and continuity energy projects demand.

So more and more organisations are choosing a more intelligent way to scale. Instead of giving up control, they add international colleagues who become part of the day-to-day work. These professionals work within your systems, follow your processes and support your team with stable capacity. Projects then run in a more structured, efficient and predictable way.
Large ambitions, limited capacity

blocks.alt: Zonnepanelen voor een industriële installatie bij zonsondergang – combinatie van fossiel en hernieuwbaar

blocks.text: Common challenges in attracting talent for the energy transition

The energy transition offers opportunities to organisations that can move quickly. Yet many teams run into the same challenge: projects grow faster than internal capacity. That puts pressure on planning, quality, continuity and the progress of projects.

items: Vacancies stay open too long.
Projects are delayed by a shortage of technical capacity.
Core teams are overloaded with operational work.
Temporary solutions are often costly and offer only a short-term answer.
Critical expertise is concentrated in a small number of staff.
Recruitment processes take longer than projects can afford.
Teams need more structure and capacity to keep projects on course.

blocks.text: With the right international professionals you strengthen your team without losing control. They work remotely as integrated colleagues, support the day-to-day work and provide the capacity needed to make durable progress.
How do you scale more intelligently?
International professionals who become part of your team

WorldEmp helps organisations in the energy transition expand their technical and operational capacity faster. We find international professionals who match your role requirements, your systems and your way of working. You keep full control. The professional works remotely within your digital working environment, follows your processes and works directly with your team on the basis of clear agreements about quality, output and collaboration.

This makes WorldEmp a strong alternative to drawn-out recruitment or traditional secondment. You build stable capacity without depending solely on the local labour market. That gives your organisation more flexibility to carry projects forward, support internal specialists and add specialist expertise exactly where it is needed.

blocks.text: Capacity without delay

The energy transition does not wait. By adding international colleagues who work remotely, you strengthen your team with extra expertise, structure and delivery power, while keeping full control over collaboration, planning and quality.
Your team keeps control. We provide the right support.

blocks.text: A more intelligent way to reach global talent
The Digital Knowledge Migrant for the energy transition

Demand for energy transition specialists keeps growing, while the availability of local talent is limited. With WorldEmp's Digital Knowledge Migrant model you gain access to highly qualified international professionals who work remotely as part of your team. They work within your digital working environment, follow your processes and contribute to your projects, without needing to relocate to the Netherlands.

This approach gives energy companies a faster, more sustainable and scalable way to strengthen their workforce. You avoid the challenges of international relocation, housing and visa procedures, while gaining access to global engineering talent for renewable energy, grid infrastructure, energy storage, hydrogen and other energy transition projects.
Why choose the Digital Knowledge Migrant model?

items: Access to international energy and engineering talent.
No relocation, housing or visa procedures.
Faster access to specialist expertise.
Less environmental impact through fewer international journeys.
Flexible and scalable capacity for growing projects.
Seamless digital collaboration as an extension of your team.
A diverse and inclusive workforce.

blocks.text: For projects and work within the energy transition
Professionals for the energy transition

According to the OECD Economic Survey of the Netherlands (2025), severe shortages of technical staff are delaying the expansion of the Dutch electricity grid and energy infrastructure. The report estimates that around 28,000 additional technical professionals are needed to meet the 2030 energy targets and to support grid expansion and the energy transition.
Some of the roles most in demand are:

items: Electrical Engineers
Power Systems Engineers
Grid Infrastructure Engineers
Project Engineers
Work Preparation Engineers
CAD & BIM Engineers
Energy Data Analysts
SCADA & Automation Engineers

blocks.text: WorldEmp helps organisations in the energy transition fill these crucial roles with experienced international professionals who become a seamless part of your team.

We discuss your technical challenge and establish the profile together, including tools, systems and specialisation.
Selection and proposal
Within a few days you receive the profile of an engineer with the right expertise and experience. You decide whether to arrange an introduction.
Kick-off and onboarding
Once agreed, we arrange a swift onboarding. The engineer works in your systems and processes, as a full member of your team.
Collaboration and quality
You stay in control. We provide clear communication, fixed points of contact and active quality control through a dedicated point of contact.
How WorldEmp adds value in your practice
Our process

items: Scoping the vacancy and aligning the role requirements with your recruitment team.
Validating the job description and technical requirements together with specialists in the field.
International sourcing through our specialist network of professionals in energy and engineering.
Screening CVs and shortlisting suitable candidates.
Assessing social skills and communication skills.
Technical interviews conducted by experienced engineering professionals.
Conversations about cultural fit and mutual expectations.
Preparing and presenting candidate profiles.
Client interviews and technical assessments, where required.
Support with the offer and the onboarding.

blocks.text: What makes WorldEmp different?

items: Access to international engineering talent.
A strong focus on communication and cultural fit.
A proven method for selecting candidates.
Professionals who integrate seamlessly into your organisation.

blocks.text: Progress calls for continuity
More focus, more capacity, more delivery power for your projects

For organisations working on the energy transition, capacity is directly tied to progress. When the right people are not available, designs, calculations, schedules and project deadlines slip. With international professionals from WorldEmp you add structural support to your team. The work keeps moving, while your internal specialists can focus on the decisions that have the most impact.

Whether your organisation works in solar, wind, hydrogen, heat, energy storage, biomass or energy supply, you need professionals who contribute to your projects consistently and dependably. WorldEmp makes scaling your workforce simpler, faster and more predictable. You keep full control of both the work and the collaboration, while we help you find international professionals who strengthen your team.

en.title: Scalable capacity for the semiconductor industry
en.description: WorldEmp helps semiconductor companies with international engineering talent and specialist professionals. Scalable technical capacity for design, quality, AI, automation and project support.

blocks.text: Supporting the growth of Dutch semiconductor companies with international talent. The Dutch semiconductor industry is in a period of strong growth. Artificial intelligence, electrification, advanced manufacturing processes and Europe's ambition to strengthen its technological independence are all driving rising investment in the semiconductor sector.
Why secondment is becoming more important in the semiconductor industry

The semiconductor industry is marked by fast growth cycles, investment in new technologies, expansion of production capacity and continuous innovation. Staffing needs can therefore change sharply in a short time, and highly specialised expertise is regularly needed for temporary projects.
Traditional recruitment processes do not always offer the flexibility organisations need for that.

Secondment makes it possible to deploy experienced professionals quickly when the need arises, which limits delays in the hiring process. That supports, among other things, the expansion of design teams, process optimisation and the implementation of new technologies.
For many organisations, secondment has grown from a temporary fix into a strategic part of their workforce strategy.
Specialist expertise for the semiconductor industry
WorldEmp supports recruitment and secondment across the full semiconductor value chain.
Design
ASIC Engineers, FPGA Engineers, Verification Engineers, Embedded Software Engineers and Physical Design Engineers who contribute to developing the next generation of chips.
Data Science & Machine Learning
Data Scientists, Machine Learning Engineers and Analytics Specialists who help organisations optimise processes, raise yields and draw valuable insight out of data.
AI & Automation
AI Engineers, Automation Specialists and Robotics Engineers who contribute to predictive maintenance, smart manufacturing and Industry 4.0 initiatives.
IT & Infrastructure
IT Infrastructure Specialists, Network Engineers, Cybersecurity Professionals and System Administrators who support technical production environments.
Quality Control
Quality Control Engineers, QC Inspectors and Quality Assurance Specialists responsible for safeguarding quality standards within production processes.
Sales
Technical Sales Engineers, Account Managers, Application Engineers and Business Development Professionals with a grasp of both customer problems and complex semiconductor technology.

blocks.text: With our secondment model, semiconductor companies gain immediate access to highly qualified professionals for project work, fab expansions and specialist assignments.
Professionals become part of your organisation, while WorldEmp remains responsible for recruitment, onboarding and support.
That lets organisations scale faster, respond flexibly to changing capacity needs and limit the long-term risks of hiring.
For permanent roles, WorldEmp supports recruitment across technical, operational and commercial disciplines.
Our selection process looks not only at technical knowledge, but at communication skills and a durable match with the organisation and its culture.

Recruitment in the semiconductor industry asks for more than a traditional recruitment approach. The sector depends on niche knowledge, specialist experience and professionals used to working within complex technical environments.
WorldEmp combines international recruitment expertise with a deep knowledge of engineering organisations and the European labour market.
Through a global talent network and a cross-border recruitment model, we help organisations reach talent beyond the ever more competitive local labour market.
We guide the full recruitment process: from sourcing and screening through to onboarding and successful integration.
A structured approach to selecting talent
Successful recruitment in the semiconductor industry goes further than matching keywords on a CV.
For roles such as AI Engineer, Automation Specialist, QC Inspector or Equipment Engineer, technical skills alone are not enough.
Successful placements also call for strong communication skills, cultural fit and the ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary engineering teams.
To limit hiring risk and make placements that last, WorldEmp follows a structured recruitment process developed specifically for technical roles.

blocks.text: This structured approach helps semiconductor companies shorten time-to-hire while improving the quality, technical fit and retention of candidates.
In specialist semiconductor roles, a careful selection process is often what separates filling a vacancy from building a team that can deliver complex projects.

blocks.text: Demand is also growing for specialists in semiconductor design, verification, AI, automation and process engineering.
International recruitment and secondment help organisations fill these specialist roles considerably faster.
Where semiconductor recruitment is heading

Competition for semiconductor talent will increase further in the coming years, driven in part by growing investment in artificial intelligence, advanced chip manufacturing and high-performance computing.
International collaboration and remote teams are becoming more common in engineering, design and digital roles, giving organisations access to expertise beyond traditional borders.
European initiatives to strengthen the local chip industry will increase demand for engineers, specialists and experienced professionals further still.
Organisations that invest in international talent pipelines and flexible workforce strategies are best prepared for these developments.
The Netherlands plays a key part in this, thanks to companies such as ASML and NXP Semiconductors and a strong network of suppliers, manufacturers and technology partners.
Introduction and understanding
We discuss your technical challenge and establish the profile together, including tools, systems and specialisation.
Selection and proposal
Within a few days you receive the profile of an engineer with the right expertise and experience. You decide whether to arrange an introduction.
Kick-off and onboarding
Once agreed, we arrange a swift onboarding. The engineer works in your systems and processes, as a full member of your team.
Collaboration and quality
You stay in control. We provide clear communication, fixed points of contact and active quality control through a dedicated point of contact.
Building the future of the semiconductor industry together
Demand for semiconductor talent is growing, while experienced professionals are getting harder to come by.

Whether you are expanding production capacity, strengthening engineering teams or looking for specialist expertise on a particular project, access to the right people at the right moment makes the difference.
WorldEmp helps semiconductor companies strengthen their teams with international recruitment, global hiring and secondment solutions that match the challenges of the semiconductor industry.
From design and quality control to AI, automation and IT infrastructure, we help organisations reach the talent they need to keep innovating, growing and delivering results.
Whether you are looking for one specialist or want to build a complete team, WorldEmp helps you find the right professionals to deliver on your ambitions.
Ready to scale up?
Daniel Perez is glad to think it through with you
I am Daniel Perez, Account Director at WorldEmp.

Every day I speak to organisations that want to grow but find technical capacity ever harder to scale. In the semiconductor industry I often see teams held up by work that has to be done but no longer fits within the core team's capacity. Together we look at where you can add capacity, which roles deliver value immediately, and how to bring in international professionals as a permanent part of your organisation.

The WorldEmp Applicant Tracking System

In today's dynamic labor market landscape, efficiency in the recruitment process is more important than ever. blocks.text: What is an Applicant Tracking System?

An Applicant Tracking System (ATS) is an advanced software application that has become indispensable in the modern recruitment landscape. This technology aids in digitalizing and streamlining the entire recruitment process. The ATS transforms how job vacancies are posted, how candidate data is managed, and how communication between recruiters and candidates is facilitated. By automating the administrative tasks involved in recruitment and selection, an ATS enables recruiters to focus on what truly matters: finding the perfect match for the team.

blocks.text: Wat is een Applicant Tracking System?

Een Applicant Tracking System (ATS) is een geavanceerde softwaretoepassing die onmisbaar is geworden in het moderne wervingslandschap. Deze technologie helpt bij het digitaliseren en stroomlijnen van het gehele wervingsproces. Het ATS transformeert de manier waarop vacatures worden geplaatst, hoe kandidaatgegevens worden beheerd en hoe communicatie tussen recruiters en kandidaten wordt gefaciliteerd. Door het automatiseren van de administratieve taken die bij werving en selectie komen kijken, stelt een ATS recruiters in staat om zich te concentreren op wat echt belangrijk is: het vinden van de perfecte match voor het team.

Flexibility and accessibility: Offers companies the ability to deploy top talent quickly and efficiently, without the logistical challenges of physical relocation.
Promotes diversity and inclusion: Facilitates a more diverse and inclusive workforce by removing borders and providing equal opportunities to talent worldwide.

blocks.html: Digitalisering van kennismigratie door WorldEmp: Een innovatieve stap richting de toekomst van werken.

items: Toegang tot wereldwijde talenten: Maakt het mogelijk voor bedrijven om hoogopgeleide professionals zoals engineers, tekenaars voor machinebouw en experts in energietransitie digitaal in te zetten.
Elimineert huisvestingsproblemen: Verwijdert de uitdagingen en kosten gerelateerd aan het vinden en financieren van geschikte huisvesting voor internationale werknemers.
Minder druk op gezondheidszorg en onderwijs: Omdat de kennismigrant niet fysiek naar Nederland komt is er geen huisarts of school voor de kinderen benodigd.
Milieuvriendelijk alternatief: Vermindert de noodzaak voor internationale reisbewegingen, wat bijdraagt aan de reductie van de carbon footprint en minder druk op het vliegverkeer legt.
Eenvoud en efficiëntie: Door het digitaliseren van de inzet van kennismigranten, versnelt en vereenvoudigt WorldEmp het proces van internationale samenwerking.
Flexibiliteit en toegankelijkheid: Biedt bedrijven de mogelijkheid om snel en efficiënt toptalent in te zetten, zonder de logistieke uitdagingen van fysieke verhuizing.
Bevordert diversiteit en inclusie: Faciliteert een meer divers en inclusief arbeidsbestand door grenzen te verwijderen en gelijke kansen te bieden aan talent wereldwijd.

blocks.text: WorldEmp's initiatief om de digitale kennismigrant te introduceren markeert een belangrijke verschuiving in hoe we denken over internationale arbeid en mobiliteit, met voordelen die verder reiken dan alleen het verminderen van bureaucratische hindernissen.

blocks.text: Wat de digitale kennismigrant voor jouw bedrijf kan betekenen

De introductie van de digitale kennismigrant door WorldEmp opent deuren naar ongekende mogelijkheden voor jouw bedrijf, ongeacht in welke sector je actief bent. Of je nu in ICT, engineering, financiën of data-analyse werkt, het toevoegen van getalenteerde internationale professionals aan je team kan de dynamiek van je projecten aanzienlijk verrijken. Dit innovatieve concept maakt het mogelijk om naadloos toegang te krijgen tot een wereldwijd reservoir van kennis en expertise, waardoor je bedrijf kan innoveren en groeien zonder de beperkingen van geografische en fysieke grenzen. De digitale kennismigrant biedt niet alleen een oplossing voor het huidige tekort aan gespecialiseerd personeel in veel sectoren, maar vermindert ook de druk op lokale middelen en bevordert een duurzamere en inclusievere werkomgeving. Door samen te werken met WorldEmp, kun je de unieke talenten en perspectieven die deze professionals meebrengen benutten om je projecten te verrijken, je innovatievermogen te vergroten en je concurrentiepositie op de internationale markt te verstevigen.

blocks.text: The role of a database administrator

Database administrators (DBAs) play an essential role in any company that relies on databases for storing and processing information. These professionals are responsible for the installation, configuration, upgrade, management, and security of databases. They ensure that data is accessible, available, and secure. DBAs perform regular backups, recover data after loss, and ensure that database systems run efficiently without interruption.
